PHYSMON | RESEARCH REDESIGN v2 (REVISED 11 NOV 2026) 1
PHYSICS-COUNTERF ACTUAL MECHANISMS
Benchmark Red-Team, DECOY-v2 Reconstruction, and a Gated Mechanistic Research
Programme
Research redesign v2 — revised edition (supersedes the edition of 14 October 2026)
PhysMon working document
11 November 2026
DOCUMENT ST A TUS.This is a proposed, falsifiable experimental protocol, not a record of experiments
performed. It is the single plan of record for PhysMon from Stage 14 onward. This edition (11 November 2026)
revises the edition of 14 October 2026 after (i) the four ICLR 2027 reviews of the Phase-I paper Confidence
Without Cause (submission 50608, withdrawn on 11 November 2026), whose numerical claims were reproduced
from the repository’s committed data; (ii) the exploratory results of Stages 14.0–14.20; (iii) a literature update
of 11 November 2026; and (iv) four independent reviews: two of a first draft (one by an agent with repository
access, one by an external language model supplied by the user) and two of the assembled draft by agents
with repository access (fidelity to the October edition and the repository; scientific consistency). The October
edition’s identifiers (B0–B7, P0–P11, A01–F20, X01–X12) are kept so that the journal, ledger and decision log
still resolve; Appendix C gives the disposition of every October block. The October PDF is preserved in Git
history (for example commit 2cf08e2).
Authorship. Revised by the project’s coding agent (Claude) at the user’s direction; checked against the
repository by independent agent reviews (Appendix D); not reviewed by a person outside the project. Revision-
sensitive hypotheses, labels, validation decisions and claim scope require explicit decision-log entries.

PHYSMON | RESEARCH REDESIGN v2 (REVISED 11 NOV 2026) 4
1 Status, scope, and rules of evidence
Purpose. An independently reasoned, falsifiable, executable research programme. The October edition
replaced the June 2026 Phase-II plan and added a mandatory benchmark red-team (Phase B). This edition
keeps that programme and changes four things, each forced by evidence gathered since: (a) the primary
endpoint is the model’s own reasoned answer, read against its sampling noise, not a teacher-forced string
likelihood; (b) the scientific question is narrowed to whether the answer follows a quantity’s certifiedphysical
roleacross values (Section4); (c) a measurement-and-calibration gate precedes every behavioural run, because
the 7–8B models are at the floor without reasoning and a 32B thinking model was near the ceiling on easy
items; (d) mechanism work declares which causal claim it tests and is read through an interaction estimand.
The target is a scientifically strong future submission, not a guarantee of acceptance.
Starting point. Phase I is the 25-page ICLR 2027 paperConfidence Without Cause: Predicting and Lo-
calizing Physics-Shortcut Sensitivity in Language Model Hidden States (submission 50608). Its four reviews
(ratings 1, 1, 3, 3; all at confidence 2) and the authors’ withdrawal on 11 November 2026 are recorded in
docs/reviews/iclr2027_submission50608/ with a script that reproduces 21 of the reviewers’ 23 checkable
claims from committed data (one computed on request, one a code reading). No Phase-I claim survives as
stated (Section2.1); its numbers remain[SUBMITTED] values. The differently titled 29-pageProved, Not
Annotated file must not be confused with the submission.
Critical epistemic constraint (unchanged). A symbolic certificate that the correct physical answer is
invariant to an edit does not prove that the model’s probability of a particular answer string ought to remain
invariant, nor does it prove use of the quantity in the model’s reasoning. Effects on probabilities, internal
representations, correct and incorrect answers, and physically faithful computation are separate estimands.S
denotes an observational sensitivity measure only;mechanism requires controlled, specific, predictive interven-
tion evidence (Section4.8); shortcut reliance is reserved for evidence that the model’s computation improperly
incorporates a quantity. This edition adds a corollary: a quantity whose influence cancels algebraically, or
depends on a regime, may legitimately enter intermediate reasoning; its use there is not an error (Section4.2).
Thesis to test, not presume. Some quantities that the physics makes irrelevant compete with relevant ones
during the model’s computation, through a structured and partially generalisable pathway. The alternatives
are legitimate outcomes and the design must be able to support each: (i) answer-string and formatting effects;
(ii) generic diﬀiculty or uncertainty; (iii) numerical copying or answer contamination without a change to
the physical computation; (iv) ordinary context sensitivity of conditional distributions; (v) several unrelated
cue-specific mechanisms; and, added in this edition, (vi) correct role selection, in which case the scientific
object becomes the mechanism of correct selection (H6). Do not design analyses that only accept the preferred
hypothesis.
Scope strategy . Phase B (Section 3) establishes what the benchmark measures. The critical path is a
sequence of gates G0–G7 (Section5.1) onto which the October blocks P0–P11 are mapped (Section5.2). The
inventory of 104 registered contrasts (Section6) remains a catalogue of candidates, not a work list. Maximise
discriminating evidence per unit of compute and human review; no unvalidated experiment enters a headline
claim after outcomes are seen.
Source categories. [SUBMITTED] = reported in the Phase-I manuscript;[REVIEW] = a criticism in
the ICLR 2027 reviews (or the earlier PAT feedback);[LITERATURE] = an independently checked public
work (Section 14); [PROPOSAL] = a new experiment, hypothesis, threshold or allocation;[V] = verified
in the repository’s committed files;[S14] = an exploratory Stage 14 result with its journal identifier;[ENV]
= a measured property of the cluster or software stack;[I] = an inference or design choice of this edition.
Numerical targets other than[SUBMITTED], [V] and [S14] values are planning choices, not results. Unlike
the October edition, this edition was written with the repository visible; every[V] and [S14] statement cites
its source.
Rules that apply at all times.
1. Data roles (EXPLORATION, GENERATOR_TUNING, INTERNAL_CONFIRMATION, EPC_CON-
FIRMATION, ADVERSARIAL_CHALLENGE) are disjoint and assigned by graph lineage; a shadow test
set is inaccessible to all tuning scripts and agents; a structure never moves from EXPLORATION into a
confirmation role.
2. The independent unit is the independently authored symbolic structure or template cluster, not a rendering,
paraphrase, numeric instantiation or decoder sample.
3. NOT_EVALUATED is not a null and notWRONG. Zero evaluable rows are not a measured zero effect. A record
that did not complete is never relabelled wrong.
4. Validation has tiers and every item states its tier: the authoring agent’s self-review is not validation;
a qualified panel of independent LLM reviewers (Section3.7) is the interim tier used for confirmation,
Working research protocol – not completed results

######## PAGE 5 ########
PHYSMON | RESEARCH REDESIGN v2 (REVISED 11 NOV 2026) 5
disclosed as such; independent human expert review is the strongest tier and is never claimed when only
the panel has run. A symbolic certificate is not a certificate of natural-language correctness.
5. Every threshold records when it was fixed relative to the data it is applied to; outcomes do not license
retroactive relabelling; new metrics are not called preregistered after the fact.
6. Every comparator is taggedoracle (needs the gold or the label’s inputs at inference) ordeployable; no
oracle comparator is called “non-activation”, “one forward pass” or “cheap”.
7. Every intervention is read as an interaction against a control prompt (Section4.8).
8. Each GPU job needs the user’s acceptance of its exact command; no job is resubmitted, cancelled or held
without it (repositoryAGENTS.md and the Sharanga skill).
2 Executive scientific judgment
The Phase-I work produced a reusable asset (a family-based benchmark with machine-checked invariance, open
per-rendering records and a decision log, which the reviewers valued) and a construct that did not survive
scrutiny. The next paper needs one of the following outcomes; which one is decided by the evidence, not chosen
in advance.
T rack M (mechanism, conditional). A verified causal account of how a quantity’s physical role is used:
which information about the quantity and its relation to the system is represented, where it travels, how it
changes the competition between the physically correct answer and a misuse-derived alternative, and which
intervention changes that dependence while preserving correct physics. Its predictions must hold on unseen
structures, values and phrasings, and replicate in a second model. It must be distinguishable from operation
planning in math word problems (Qu and Gomes), anchoring pathways (Owusu et al.) and positional readout
copying (Liu). A single exceptional component is insuﬀicient. Track M may also be aboutcorrect selection
(H6) if the models select correctly.
T rack E (evaluation and measurement). A rigorous decomposition of which apparent “shortcut” signals
are artifacts of reference-answer scoring, prompt formatting, metric asymmetry or data structure, and which
survive as reproducible violations of certified role-by-value behaviour. Phase I and Stage 14 already supply
much of the artifact side (Section2.1, AppendixA). Track E must not claim a mechanism.
T rack R (robustness and repair, optional). A selective intervention that improves certified invariance or
accuracy on unseen data, with little damage to legitimate use of relevant quantities, and an advantage over
cheap baselines (a relevance instruction, self-consistency, a longer reasoning budget).
Three questions that precede expensive mechanism work (sharpened from the October edition): (1)
Does the model’s answer follow the certified role-by-value pattern, measured on its own reasoned answers
rather than on a teacher-forced string? (2) Is any departure specific to the physical role, rather than to numeral
presence, plausibility, unit, position, marker wording or generic perturbation, and is it specific to physics rather
than shared with non-physics dependency problems? (3) Does an identified computation generalise beyond
the selection panel? If any answer is no, the corresponding stronger vocabulary is not used.

What survives. Descriptive facts: the teacher-forced gold-string likelihood moves with the choice of base
rendering, with the answer instruction, with in-context answer information and with the scoring string. These
support Track E’s methodological point and nothing stronger.
2.2 What Stage 14 established (exploratory)
All Stage 14 results have data role EXPLORATION and are not paper-eligible; details and identifiers are
in Appendix A. In brief: [S14] a same-unit numeral in the prompt becomes a far more probable answer
continuation (about 10–13 nats for Qwen2.5-7B, 3.5–5 for Llama-3.1-8B), with no detectable dependence on
Working research protocol – not completed results

######## PAGE 7 ########
PHYSMON | RESEARCH REDESIGN v2 (REVISED 11 NOV 2026) 7
proximity at the available precision; matching comparison numerals for plausibility removes about 40% (Qwen)
and 53% (Llama) of it, leaves incompatible-unit and metadata effects not distinguishable from plausibility, and
leaves a remainder that depends on unit compatibility (J14.9, J14.14, J14.17). Without reasoning both 7–8B
models are almost never correct (3/211, 6/211); with greedy 2,048-token reasoning Qwen is correct on 96/211
and Llama on 50/211, but a sentence with no number changes answers about as often as numeric cues (J14.7,
J14.13). Qwen3-32B with thinking answered 63 of 64 graded problems on one sample each; four cue kinds
on 32 of those candidate anchors left 109 of 111 graded answers correct, with 17 of 128 cellsNOT_EVALUATED;
the resample that would have measured its own noise was cancelled, so its cue contrast isNOT_EVALUATED
(J14.19-009 to -015). None of this tests the role-by-value question; the cues in these runs also carried explicit
disclaimers (“unrelated”, “not connected”) in the prompt text.
3 A mandatory Phase B: red-team, reconstruct, and independently
validate DECOY
This section keeps the October edition’s Phase B (v2.0, pp. 4–13): the board decision, the benchmark archi-
tecture, blocks B0–B7 with their numbered sub-items, and Gates B1–B6. Identifiers are unchanged so that
Stage 14 journal entries (J14.x-nnn), the claim ledger and the first revision (v2.1) still resolve. What has
changed is where each requirement now lives. The construct choice that v2.0 left open (B2) is decided in
Section 4; the pilot, confirmation and external work of B5–B7 are re-sequenced into the critical path of Sec-
tion 5.1 (G0 integrity closure; G1 physics construct; G2 measurement and model calibration; G3 behavioural
discovery; G4 independent behavioural confirmation; G5 mechanism; G6 external and functional confirmation;
G7 optional practical use). Where this section and Section4 disagree, Section4 wins.

3.1 The board decision and its reasons
Board decision (14 October 2026) [PROPOSAL]. Do not use the existing 155-family DECOY benchmark
unchanged as the sole scientific foundation of a future PhysMon mechanism claim. Do not discard its Phase-I
evidence, and do not substitute a pre-existing public physics benchmark wholesale. Maintain an immutable
DECOY-v1 (historical reproduction and failure diagnosis); conditionally build a DECOY-v2 experimental suite
for controlled causal discovery; establish a separately sourced, separately certified External Physics Counter-
Working research protocol – not completed results

######## PAGE 8 ########
PHYSMON | RESEARCH REDESIGN v2 (REVISED 11 NOV 2026) 8
factuals (EPC) collection for confirmation; and use GSM-DC and GSM-Symbolic as non-physics controls.
Treat unit and re-expression invariance as a distinct task, not interchangeable with irrelevant numerical cues.
Neither a large newly generated dataset nor an improved AUROC makes the work valuable unless these tests
establish a precise, nontrivial model behaviour and an independently validated causal explanation.
Three questions that precede expensive mechanism work. (1) Does the claimed behaviour survive
scoring and task-formulation challenges? (2) Is any internal effect specific to the manipulated physical role
rather than a generic output perturbation? (3) Does the identified computation generalise beyond the selection
panel? If any answer is no, the corresponding stronger vocabulary is not used.
Scientific reasons (each a reported property or a falsification target, not a finding that v2 has succeeded).
(i) The original signed base-relative sensitivity label can change when the same four renderings are re-indexed.
(ii) A certificate about a symbolic answer value does not constrain the probability of a chosen answer string,
and physical assumptions asserted in natural language are not checked by free-symbol elimination. (iii) Cue C
changes how a governing quantity is expressed; it does not add physically irrelevant information. (iv) Five
original Cue C families, 34 structure clusters, 2,352 unresolved cross-family rendering pairs, no completed
independent expert validation, and a 135-family monitoring cohort with outcome-related filtering limit infer-
ence [SUBMITTED]. (v) GSM-Symbolic and GSM-DC already establish controlled irrelevant-context tests;
novelty cannot be “symbolic templates plus distractors”[LITERATURE].
Status (11 Nov 2026): in force; reasons (i)–(iv) since verified. (i) X02: of the legacy base-0 positives,
40–49% (Qwen) and 41–56% (Llama) turn negative under another base (J14.2-006); the label also agrees at
chance across two answer instructions on the 30 pilot families (Spearman 0.043, 17 of 30) and scores the bare
certified string rather than the instructed format[REVIEW]. (ii) A correct formula hint raises the gold-string
log-probability by 3.7–5.5 nats on five stable families[REVIEW]; the v1 verifier has no Cue C identity or
dimension check [REVIEW]. (iii) Cue C pooling was raised by three of four reviewers (issue 9). (iv) The 34
clusters were rebuilt from the committed leakage table (J14.4-002). REVISED: the decision’s single notion of
an “irrelevant” cue is replaced by the four role strata R, D, C, K of Section4.2.

Strict version policy (unchanged). Any semantic revision of a governing equation, assumption, target
variable, accepted answer or cue role increments the family’s (now: the structure’s) version; nothing is edited
silently in place. Source dataset revisions and hashes are frozen. Once a confirmatory panel is opened it is not
used to tune generation rules, architecture, scoring, parsers, thresholds, site selection or eligibility. Negative
and ineligible examples stay in an immutable manifest with reasons.[PROPOSAL] Under the role-by-value
design a stratum assignment, a role phrasing, a certified responsey∗ r (z) and a misuse-function list are semantic
content of the structure and fall under the same rule.
3.3 B0. Benchmark threat model, estimand map and external novelty audit
Status (11 Nov 2026): REVISED and PARTIAL. B0.1 and B0.2 are absorbed into Section4; B0.3 is partly
covered by the review issue register and Stage 14; B0.4 is now Section11; the standalone B0 threat file and
red-team protocol are OPEN.
B0.1 What the benchmark is not. The certified statement concerns the physical mappingy∗ = f (r, a); it
is not a statement about equal conditional model probabilitiespθ(string(y∗) | xi, q). An answer-invariant pair
establishes a correct response target, not the model’s computation or its internal dependence on a nuisance. No
label is named shortcut reliance without controlled behavioural and mechanism evidence. Separate records are
kept for (a) physical target invariance, (b) observed gold-string drift, (c) actual-answer shift, (d) distractor-
derived answer preference, (e) erroneous dependency on a physical cue, (f) a causal internal component or
pathway. Now: (a) is the stratum certificate (Section4.2); (b) is a retired endpoint (Section4.5); (c) and (d)
are O1–O4, with misuse curves rather than single decoy matches (Section4.3); (e) needs H3 or H4 established
under T2 or T3 (Sections4.7, 4.8); (f) is a claim type of Section4.8.
B0.2 F ormal object. A task stores physical states, assumptionsa, a dependency graph or programg, target
t, physical answery∗(s, a, t), candidate cuez, semantic roleR(z), perturbation operatorI and renderingR. A
nuisance intervention satisfiesy∗(Iz(s), a, t) = y∗(s, a, t) within a declared domainD; a relevant intervention is
a positive control whose transformed target is computed, including cases where the numerical answer happens
to coincide despite true dependence. Role is never established by answer-value coincidence alone: a variable
Working research protocol – not completed results

######## PAGE 10 ########
PHYSMON | RESEARCH REDESIGN v2 (REVISED 11 NOV 2026) 10
can be causally relevant at a parameter setting with zero local effect.Now: the four strata make this precise:
D by graph disconnection, C by an identically zero derivative, K by a regime predicate with a documented
counter-regime value, R by a certified response curve over a declared range ofm ≥ 3 values (Sections4.2, 4.3).
The last sentence of B0.2 is the reason K is its own stratum and why a single R value never certifies relevance.
B0.3 Preregistered threat taxonomy . Audits attack: incorrect physical semantics, missing boundary
conditions, excluded-domain exceptions, dimensional and unit errors, answer-rounding ambiguities, canonical
strings and tokens, no-cue anchor dependence, arbitrary base choice, irrelevant numerical value versus extra
text, prompt wrapper and generation position, template or source overlap, near-match selection, cue-condition
class prevalence, sampling and decoder variation, annotator suggestion and automation bias, architecture-
specific scoring incompatibility, adaptive head selection, data contamination and publication novelty. Each
risk receives a test, an accountable owner, a possible failure class and an action.Status: PARTIAL. Tested
on v1 or v2 records: canonical string and wrapper (J14.3-003, J14.10-005; review check C1[REVIEW]), base
choice (J14.2-006), template overlap (J14.4), near-match selection (review check C7; J14.17-006), automation
bias (agent authorship of all 155 v1 templates, review check C9; agent verification of the v2 set, J14.19-
001). The ICLR issue register lists 20 issues, of which 16 were already prescribed by v2.0, 3 partly and 1 is
writing hygiene [REVIEW]. Not yet tested on v2 items: contamination, sampling variation under a sampled
contract (G2), novelty (Section11). Threats added since v2.0: role marker words in the prompt (B2.3 status),
selection and estimation on the same samples (J14.19-014), and budget exhaustion read as a wrong answer
(O3, Section4.5).
B0.4 Closest-work matrix. For each close work record: dependency program, control of nuisance and
relevant edits, formal guarantee, human semantics review, diﬀiculty, output metrics, intervention capability,
public data and derivation, external transfer. The differentiator must hold as a joint contribution (physical-role
interventions, honest behavioural endpoints, mechanistic prediction with causal rescue, external confirmation);
v2 is never called novel because it is larger than v1.Status: REVISED; now Section11. v2.0’s list (GSM-
Symbolic, GSM-DC, UGPhysics, PhysReason, PHYSICS-Verified, mechanism papers) is kept and extended;
the closest named works are now PRISM-Physics, GSM-DC, Qu and Gomes, Owusu, Wiegreffe and Feldman,
and Liu (“The Readout Shortcut”). The absence of a matching benchmark in our search is not proof of novelty
(Section 4.1).
Deliverable B0: aversioned benchmark_claims_and_threats.md, aclosest-worktablewithaccessibleURLs,
an estimand glossary and an independent red-team protocol.Status: the glossary is Sections4.5 and 4.8; the
table is Section11; the threat file (owner and action per threat) and the independent red-team protocol are
OPEN and belong with G0[PROPOSAL].
F ailure branch (kept). If physical relevance cannot be distinguished from GSM-DC-style dependency se-
lection, the research is framed as generic numerical interference or dependency selection, with physics as a
controlled domain, and no physics-specific relevance computation is claimed. It is now tested early by the
non-physics dependency control of G3 and fully in G6.

3.5 B2. Decide the construct before choosing how many examples to generate
Status (11 Nov 2026): REVISED (decided). The construct is fixed in Section4 (research question, strata,
role-by-value design, outcomes, populations, hypotheses). B2.3 and B2.4 remain binding rules and are restated
below with their new connections.
B2.1 Hypothesis families. v2.0 defined H-P (physical relevance selection), H-N (numerical interference),
H-T (text and interface effects on a single reference string) and H-U (unit and representation transformations),
and forbade pooling H-U with the others.Now (Section 4.7): H-N becomes H1 and H2; H-P becomes H3, H4
and H6; H-T is the retired string construct plus the position and format controls; H-U is the convertible-unit
Working research protocol – not completed results

######## PAGE 12 ########
PHYSMON | RESEARCH REDESIGN v2 (REVISED 11 NOV 2026) 12
family (V2-B). The pooling ban is generalised: results are never pooled across role strata (Section4.2, rule 3).
B2.2 Primary behaviour as an interpretable contrast. v2.0 conditions: (i) no cue, (ii) irrelevant cue
of varying magnitude, (iii) style-matched non-numerical text, (iv) generic numerical metadata, (v) relevant
edit with recomputed gold, (vi) adversarially constructed decoy answer; co-endpoints were decoy-candidate
probability and free-answer correctness, with one primary endpoint chosen after the pilot.Now: (ii) becomes
the D, C and K cells atm ≥ 3 values; (v) becomes the R cell with a certified response (and the relevant edit of
an existing input stays as a supporting condition); (vi) becomes the prespecified misuse functionsfh(z) with
all matches kept; (i), (iii), (iv) are supporting conditions (Sections4.3, 4.4). The primary scientific endpoint
is O4; O1, O2, O3 and O5 are always reported; candidate log-odds (O6) exist only inside a causal claim type;
teacher-forced dispersion is a diagnostic (Section4.5). G4 confirms the role-by-value family fixed in advance
(Section 5.1); the G3 scorecard may add at most one secondary family, labelled as chosen on EXPLORATION
data.
B2.3 Relevance is not a keyword (binding). Match tasks with explicitly disconnected and physically
connected subsystems, but do not fabricate a single-word role flip that changes other physical assumptions or
allows several plausible readings. Every pair gets its own formal state change, recomputed solution and expert
semantic validation (B4). Add subtle relevance that requires causal tracing (an intermediate variable changes
only through an indirect coupling) beside explicitly stated irrelevance, to tell relevance computation from a
memorised “isolated” or “ignore”.Connection to the strata: the explicitly disconnected case is stratum D; the
connected case and the indirect-coupling case are stratum R; strata C and K are the hard non-keyword cases
in which the quantity sits inside the target system (Section4.2). The role-by-value design implements the rule
by requiring at least two independently validated phrasings of each role relation, at least one without marker
words such as “unrelated” or “separate”, and agreement across phrasings before any role claim (Section4.3).
Status: the Stage 14 items do not meet this rule for role claims: of 1,464 feasible non-governing cells in
dataset v1, 1,085 say the quantity is “unrelated”, 39 “not connected”, 11 “takes no part”, 9 “in a separate
experiment” and the rest use other separating wording, so the prompt itself states the role (v2.1, §5.1). Those
records bear on presence and unit effects (J14.14-005, J14.17-006), not on role selection.
B2.4 Eligibility strata before scoring (binding). Report all valid problems (intent-to-evaluate), format-
parseable records (only for metrics that truly need parsing), base-correct items, and model-positive items
(eligible for sensitivity reduction or causal recovery), each with its denominator and selection mechanism.
A result conditional on base correctness is not a general result about all questions; the original signed ef-
fect never substitutes for the question whether the model outputs an incorrect answer.Connection to the
populations (Section 4.6): all valid problems is the population “all validated tasks” and is always reported;
format-parseability is no longer a population but the status outcome O3, and a record that is notCOMPLETE
is never relabelled wrong; base-correct is “tasks solved reliably without a cue”, which needs repeated samples
(one correct sample makes a candidate anchor only, J14.19-009); model-positive items are a sub-population
used only inside G5 and G7 with their selection stated. The calibrated intermediate-diﬀiculty population is
new (G2), and its selection samples are never reused for estimation. Every result names both its role stratum
and its population.
B2.5 Metric calibration and negative controls. Kept: absolute differences and robust quantiles; no
ranking of architectures by the share crossing 0.5 nats; a permitted null distribution of cue-free and formatting-
only changes, now the sampling baseline (self-flip floor from fresh no-cue samples) of G2 together with the
style-matched non-numeric sentence; the no-cue reference is not called universally neutral until the omission-
versus-added-text asymmetry is tested, which the non-numeric sentence does. Symmetric range, first-token
and full-sequence scores and varied output strings are diagnostics; output-format sensitivity is also covered by
the three grading views (Section4.5). The legacy signed label is retired.
Gate B2 (v2.0). If H-P or H-N produces reliable behaviour beyond generic text and answer-string effects, proceed
to a narrow causal benchmark emphasising that phenomenon. If only H-T survives, create a measurement and LM-
interface project and freeze physics-reliance claims. If only H-U survives, split it into a formal equivariance study, not
the core programme. If all effects disappear under realistic controls, archive a carefully documented negative result
and do not manufacture additional distractor conditions to force a positive headline.
Status: REPLACED as a decision rule by the G3 hypothesis scorecard over H0–H6 (Section5.1). Its branches
correspond: H-P or H-N reliable→ H1–H4 readings; only H-T→ readout and interface claims of type T1 only;
only H-U → the separate equivariance study; everything absent→ H0 reported as a null with its equivalence
bounds and power. Its last sentence stays in force without change.

3.6 B3. A modular v2 benchmark with mutually discriminating controls
Status (11 Nov 2026): REVISED (extended with the role strata and the role-by-value cells). The typed
generator and 80 structures exist (DONE-EXPLORATORY: J14.6, J14.15, J14.18, J14.19); strata C and K,
role-by-value cells, validated phrasings and misuse functions are OPEN and belong to G1.
B3.1 Five problem-structure strata (kept). (i) Single governing equation with a natural nuisance (cali-
bration and causal simplicity); (ii) multistep dependency graph with the distractor attached to a non-ancestor
node; (iii) interacting subsystems with an explicit or inferable physical disconnection; (iv) conditional laws or
boundary constraints where relevance depends on a stated regime; (v) counterfactual role reversal, where the
same measured quantity is relevant in one verified world and irrelevant in another. Include inverse problems
and sign or vector questions where answer and representation validation are reliable. Do not assume ther-
modynamics or multimodal diagrams are easy to certify; admit only validated examples and keep excluded
candidates in a selection log. Extension. Problem structure and role stratum are two axes: each structure
records its problem-structure stratum and which role strata it admits; infeasibility is recorded, never imputed
(Section 4.3). Typical, not definitional, correspondences: (i) often yields C (e.g. a pulley radius that cancels
when the moment of inertia is given as a fraction ofM R2) or D; (ii) yields D for a non-ancestor node and
R for an ancestor; (iii) yields R/D twins; (iv) yields K; (v) is the role-by-value design itself (R and D cells
of one structure at the same values). The Stage 14role_reversal cell changes the question (the answer
minus system B’s value), so it tests use on request, not role with the question fixed (v2.1, §5.1); it stays as the
supporting condition “role reversal (use on request)” and does not implement (v).
B3.2 Typed executable graph generator. Each node stores dimension, unit, reference frame, sign con-
vention, quantity type, provenance (measured, computed, assumed), uncertainty where relevant and parent
edges; each structure has a solver program and a small proof object (assumptions, symbolic identities, rele-
vance certificate, admissible cue domain, tested boundary cases); hard instances are checked by more than one
route, not by several outputs of one symbolic generator.Status: DONE-EXPLORATORY for the v2.0 scope:
dimensional checker, typed DAG, eleven-check certifier, proof object, mutation harness and independently
coded solvers (J14.6-001, J14.6-007); 80 structures in 11 domains with gold traces rendered from the graph
(J14.19-002, J14.19-003). Blind-solver agents are a further route of the same model family, not an independent
one (J14.19-001). REVISED[PROPOSAL]: the Stage 14 generator keeps nuisance quantities out of the graph
(J14.6-001), which can certify D-type absence only. Strata C and K need the quantity inside the governing
relations, with certified symbolic cancellation (C) or a regime predicate and counter-regime value (K); R needs
a certified responsey∗ R(z) over the declared range, separated fromy∗ D(z) by more than the loosest tolerance;
every D, C and K cell also needs its frozen misuse functionsfh(z) (Sections 4.2, 4.3). This is G1 work.
B3.3 Core interaction. v2.0 crossed physical relevance (governing versus non-governing), numerical proxim-
ity (near-match versus a predeclared far band) and unit relationship (same or equivalent versus incompatible),
with diagnostic cells separating digit overlap from magnitude (close magnitudes with little lexical overlap; far
magnitudes with shared leading digits; equal numerals with incompatible units; unit-compatible far distrac-
tor; unit-incompatible but lexically overlapping distractor), cluster-level inference, and empty or impossible

B3.4 F actor families expanded only after the core signal. Placement and recency, ordering, num-

3.7 B4. Human validation as an independent scientific experiment
Status (11 Nov 2026): OPEN; requirements unchanged. No independent validator exists and none has
been qualified. Validator-qualification materials (v2) and a 33-item planted-defect bank exist (J14.5); the user
reviewed the bank (27 items defective as declared, 6 valid controls; J14.5-013) as one non-blinded reviewer
who did not state physics expertise, so physicist confirmation of the bank is open. S01–S20 had the user’s
open walkthrough. On 2026-10-26 the user directed agent verification (author, blind-solver and plan-reviewer
agents) in place of the physicist review (J14.19-001): all 80 v2 structures carry admission categoryUNREVIEWED
with an agent-verification record, and no text may call them expert-reviewed. Agent checks share the authors’
model family and can share their blind spots (J14.19-001). For v1, all 155 templates were created by an agent
and 140 were marked validated through a delegated agent review[REVIEW]; the reviewers’ objection to this
(issue 10) applies equally to the v2 set.Consequence: no structure has passed Gate B4.
Interim validation tier: a qualified LLM review panel (user direction, 11 November 2026). Recruiting
independent physicists takes time the project does not want to spend now, so confirmation (G4) uses a panel
of independent LLM reviewers as the interim validation tier, and human expert review is a later study that
measures the panel and can upgrade items.
1. Panel. Two to three judge models from model families other than the authoring model (Claude), and
where possible from different families from each other, at least one a strong reasoning model; the panel
composition, versions and prompts are frozen in G1 (open decision D2 now asks which models). The
authoring agent is never on the panel, and neither are models from the families under test (Qwen, Llama);
a judge never sees another judge’s verdict, any model-under-test output or score, or the study hypotheses,
in either pass, and does not see the gold trace in its first pass.
2. Protocol. The B4.2 two-pass rubric, run per judge: pass 1 solves the problem and states each quantity’s role
stratum from the text alone; pass 2 checks the certificate claims (stratum, invariance or certified response,
units, assumptions, naturalness, whether the renderings differ only as intended) and returns a structured
verdict with severity and reasons.
3. Qualification before use. Each judge, with its frozen prompt, is run on the 33-item planted-defect bank
(27 defective and 6 valid controls, labelled by the user, J14.5-013) and must meet thresholds fixed in G1
(planning: detect at least 85% of the defective items for the declared reason and accept at least 5 of the 6
Working research protocol – not completed results

######## PAGE 15 ########
PHYSMON | RESEARCH REDESIGN v2 (REVISED 11 NOV 2026) 15
valid ones). Because six valid controls estimate false rejection very imprecisely, G1 adds freshly generated
valid items and new planted defects to the bank before qualification, and holds a portion out unseen; a
judge or prompt changed after seeing bank results is requalified only on that held-out portion or on a fresh
planted set. The bank is not used to tune prompts.
4. Admission rule. An item is LLM_PANEL_VALIDATED when every qualified judge accepts it with no high-
severity defect; split verdicts go to a recorded adjudication whose adjudicator and tier are stated (the user,
who labelled the bank, is not an independent adjudicator), and adjudicated items are reported separately;
itemswithanyunresolvedhigh-severityflagareexcludedandcounted. Agreementstatistics(rawagreement,
Cohen’s κ, Gwet’s AC1) are reported as for human validators.
5. Claim language. G4 results on panel-validated items are “confirmatory under LLM-panel validation”; no
text calls them expert-validated; agent authorship and LLM validation are disclosed.
6. Human study later. A stratified sample of panel verdicts (accepted, rejected, split) is later reviewed by
independent humans (G6 or P11) to estimate the panel’s error rates; items that pass are upgraded to the
expert tier.
Without a qualified panel, G4 is run but labelled EXPLORATORY-REPLICATION, and no text calls it
confirmatory.
B4.1 Audit before claiming certified English. Every v1 family gets at least one qualified blinded se-
mantics review, and every family used in a publishable confirmatory claim gets two independent reviews with
third-party adjudication where needed; the validation pilot samples across cue types, physics domains, largest
likelihood shifts, negative scores, presumed easy cases, ambiguous coupled systems and high-overlap clusters;
authors never self-certify the semantic naturalness of their own families.Now: the v1 part applies only if v1 is
reused; the two-review rule applies to every G4 structure and every adapted EPC item (interim: the qualified
LLM panel of Section3.7), and sampling for the pilot also spans the role strata.
B4.2 T wo-pass review instrument. Pass 1, without the authors’ equation: solve or outline the physics,
state assumptions and target, whether the cue could affect the target, and whether the wording permits another
physical reading. Pass 2, with the encoded graph and certificate: check graph, units, domain, numerical
answer, cues and any omitted dependency. Validity, clarity, diﬀiculty and naturalness are judged separately;
uncertainty is marked and counterexamples annotated.[PROPOSAL] Under the strata, Pass 1 also asks the
reviewer to assign the quantity’s stratum (R, D, C, K) blind and, for K, to state the regime; Pass 2 checks
the stratum certificate, the certified response or invariance range, the misuse functions and each role phrasing
separately.
B4.3 Qualification and independence. Screen reviewers with calibrated problems including boundary-
condition traps, unit conversions and misleading “isolated” claims; record expertise by domain; balance assign-
ments across authors, sources, cue types and diﬀiculty; reviewers are blind to model outcomes and to probe or
circuit hypotheses; estimate payment and time in a small pilot, then resource the whole set. Disagreements go
to a domain-qualified independent third reviewer. Agreement is reported as raw agreement, Cohen’s kappa on
substantive claims, uncertainty intervals and category-specific defect rates, with unresolved ambiguities listed.
B4.4 Adversarial validation tests. Before release insert predeclared planted defects (hidden coupling, miss-
ing assumption, relevant variable removed from the equation, failed transformation identity, inconvertible or
inconsistent units, invalid parameter domain, insuﬀicient boundary condition, invalid precision, contradictory
distractor statement) and a valid equivalent rewrite; measure detection sensitivity and false-rejection rate by
mutation type; if reviewers miss a defect type, revise the checklist and recalibrate before confirmation. The
planted bank never enters the benchmark as genuine physics.
B4.5 Admission categories. CERTIFIED_AND_VALIDATED, SOLVER_VALID_LANGUAGE_AMBIGUOUS, SOLVER_-
INVALID, ANSWER_AMBIGUOUS, NATURALNESS_FLAG, REVISED_REVALIDATED, EXCLUDED, UNREVIEWED. Report
fractions before and after repair; store a signed reviewer record; never count repaired examples as untouched
independent examples; publish the protocol and aggregate outcomes without reviewers’ personal identifiers.
Agent verification is recorded beside these categories and never changesUNREVIEWED.
Gate B4 (unchanged). Confirmatory physical-relevance claims are blocked until independent expert semantic vali-
dation, version-correct solver checks and the parser criterion for the relevant endpoint pass. No arbitrary agreement
threshold substitutes for reviewing concrete physics defects. High disagreement or mutation-test failure means a new
validation cycle, not optimistic averaging.

Why the hybrid design matters. Public benchmarks supply diversity and independent authorship but not

v2 and adapted public questions serve different causal and generalisation purposes.

B5.1 Outcome-independent sampling. Per source document revision, inclusion criteria, population, seed,
subject and answer-type strata, sampling probabilities, original id and provenance, removed figures and reuse
constraints. Never pick the published problems a model fails and adapt the dramatic ones for a “representative”
external test.
B5.2 Conversion pipeline. (1) identify the original target and material assumptions; (2) solve independently
orreconstructanexecutabledependencyprogram; (3)identifysafeinterventionpointsandcandidatequantities
(now: candidate quantities for each feasible stratum); (4) derive the output under both edits (now: the certified
response or invariance over the declared values); (5) preserve essential semantics; (6) independent physics and
naturalness review of each adapted pair; (7) audit overlap with v1 and v2 and training-contamination risk; (8)
freeze adapted items and scoring before evaluating models. Reason-coded rejections are logged at each step.
B5.3 F easibility pilot. A precommitted, stratified 20–40-candidate sample from each of PHYSICS-Verified
and UGPhysics, optionally a smaller PhysReason sample; measure adaptation yield, reviewer hours, certifi-
cation rate, diﬀiculty and baseline solve rate, with intervals on yield and a representativeness comparison of
retained and rejected items. It decides source suitability; it is not an external test.
B5.4 Independent external sets. (i) EPC-D, an adapted development set that may inform methods and
tooling but never confirms an already tuned claim; (ii) EPC-C, a locked confirmation set authored, adapted
and verified by different staff after the target and code are frozen; (iii) EPC-N, new expert-authored problems
not derived from public benchmarks, against contamination and reference leakage. Aim for heterogeneity
across law, source and diﬀiculty rather than more paraphrases. The final external set is opened once; any
revision after a failure needs a new independent set.
B5.5 Source- and solvability-aware estimands. Report all eligible cases, base-correct cases and the
available physically meaningful wrong-answer alternatives; if small models fail hard items, disclose the selection
and the shifted population instead of keeping only successes; use relevant-edit responsiveness (now the R-cell
response, O4) even without baseline correctness; verify native unit and answer scoring for each model before
comparing them.

B5.6 Cross-domain falsification. Select abstractly matched GSM-DC and GSM-Symbolic structures, mea-
sure interference under their own validated protocols, then evaluate a carefully translated subset under Phys-

equivalent grade-school arithmetic, read the mechanism as general dependency filtering or numerical copying
unless a truly physics-specific manipulation separates them. Split: the small control in G3 gives the early
behavioural reading; the full version, including mechanism transfer, is G6.
Gate B5 (kept; now applied in G6). If adaptations are rare or ambiguous, preserve source rejection rates and either
restrict the external question types or commission independent expert-authored tasks; never downgrade certification
to inflate numbers. If only synthetic tasks show effects, make that limitation central and do not claim broad physics
reasoning. Confirmed external effects are required for a broad generalisation claim.

4 The falsifiable theoretical framework
This section is the construct specification for all work from Stage 15 onward. It replaces the construct choice
left open by the October edition (B2, Section3) with a decision, and it is the reference that every later section
uses for endpoints, strata and causal claims.
4.1 Research question and scoped claim
Primary question. When a physics problem contains a quantity whose role in the target computation is
certified, does the model’s answer depend on that quantity in the way the physics requires — invariant when
the quantity is irrelevant, responsive by the certified amount when it is relevant — beyond what is explained
by the numeral’s presence, its value and plausibility, its unit, its position, the wording that marks its role and
generic perturbation of the text? If the dependence departs from the physics, which computation produces
the departure; and if it follows the physics, which computation implements the selection?
Secondary question. Does reasoning (thinking on versus off within the same weights, and the reasoning
budget) change how role is used, and is a quantity’s cost paid in correctness, in length, or in failures to finish?
Scoped claim. PhysMon proposes to distinguishnumerical salience from physical dependency through in-
dependently validated counterfactual manipulations of a quantity’s physical role and value, and then to test
whether that distinction has an identifiable causal implementation in a language model. The absence of a
matching benchmark in our literature search (Section11) is not proof of novelty; the claim is made against the
closest named works: PRISM-Physics (physics formula DAGs and process-level scoring), GSM-DC (symbolic
dependency graphs with irrelevant nodes), Qu and Gomes (a mechanistic account of math distractor failure),
Owusu, Wiegreffe and Feldman (anchoring pathways), and Liu (positional readout copying). A PhysMon
result that one of these already explains is reported as such, not as a new phenomenon.
4.2 What “irrelevant” means: four role strata
Physical irrelevance is not one property. A quantity’s role is one of four strata, each with its own certificate and
its own correct behaviour. The October edition’s single “non-governing cue” and the first revision’s “in-system
inert quantity” both conflated the last three.

Rules. (1) A model’s internal representation of a quantity, attention to it, or its use in an intermediate step
is never classified as an error merely because the final answer is invariant to that quantity; for strata C and K
such use can be correct physics. (2) Error claims are made only about outputs (the final answer’s behaviour
across values, Section4.3) or about intermediate steps whose wrongness is certified against the graph. (3)
Each stratum is a separate benchmark stratum with its own hypotheses (Section4.7); results are never pooled
across strata. (4) Stratum D is the only stratum in which “the quantity should not enter the computation” is
the expectation.
4.3 The role-by-value design (scientific centrepiece)
A single relevant/irrelevant twin cannot separate role from diﬀiculty (the relevant twin may need more steps)
or from a lexical marker (“separate system” means “ignore”). The primary design therefore crosses role and
value within each structure.
For a quantity q in structure s, with values z1, . . . , zm (m ≥ 3 in every run, so that misuse curves are
identifiable; m ≥ 5 with held-out values for the dependency-curve test), roler ∈ {R, D, C, K} where feasible,
and at least two independently validated phrasingsp of each role relation (at least one without marker words
such as “unrelated” or “separate”), the generator certifiesy∗ r (z) for every cell. Correct physics requires
y∗ D(z1) = y∗ D(z2) (and likewise forC, K), y ∗ R(z2) − y∗ R(z1) = ∆ ∗ R ̸= 0.
Two questions are then asked at once: is the model invariant where the physics says it must be, and does it
respond by the correct amount where the quantity is relevant?
Estimands defined on sampled answers. Answers are a mixture of correct values, wrong values and
non-complete records, so no single “answer” per cell exists; the estimands are built to survive that.
1. Tracking (primary, per sample): T = 1 if the sample is COMPLETE and its value lies within the declared
tolerance of the certifiedy∗ r (z) of its own cell, elseT = 0, over all attempted samples; the complete-case
versionisasensitivityanalysis. Perstructure, ¯Tr averagesovervalues, phrasingsandsamples. Inappropriate
dependence in D (and C, K) is the tracking loss¯TN − ¯TD against the token-aligned non-numeric sentence
N at the same position, so that generic distraction by an added sentence is not counted as role failure (the
loss against the no-cue prompt is reported beside it): a departure ineither direction (adding, subtracting,
copying or any other use of the quantity) that moves the answer outside the tolerance lowers tracking, so
this measure has no blind sign.Responsivenessis ¯TR.
2. Answer-mode shares (primary for attribution, per sample): the share of samples whose value matches each
prespecified misuse curvefh(z) in D, C and K cells (misuse shares), and the share of R samples whose value
Working research protocol – not completed results

######## PAGE 21 ########
PHYSMON | RESEARCH REDESIGN v2 (REVISED 11 NOV 2026) 21
matches the irrelevant-role answery∗ D(z), i.e. that ignore a quantity that matters (neglect share). A misuse
share in a D, C or K cell is compared with the rate at which the non-numeric controlN at the same z
produces the same value; a misuse curve is supported only when its share exceeds that rate at two or more
of at least three values. The neglect share cannot useN or the no-cue prompt as comparator (their correct
answer is y∗ D(z)); it is compared with a placebo match rate in the same R cell, the share of R samples equal
to a prespecified placebo value2y∗ R(z) − y∗ D(z) (as far from the correct answer as the neglect value, on the
other side), certified to be separated from the gold and every foil; where that value is physically impossible
(for example negative for a positive-definite quantity), the generator uses a prespecified multiplicative offset
of the same size instead, so that the placebo is as plausible as the neglect value. The misuse set contains
signed variants (add and subtract the quantity; substitute it; copy it; for C and K the wrong law or wrong
regime), each with the direction of its prediction stated in advance.
3. Normalised response fraction (descriptive only): λr = [ mr(zb) − mr(za)]/[y∗ R(zb) − y∗ R(za)] for each value
pair, with mr the Hodges–Lehmann location of theCOMPLETE answers of the cell (robust to isolated unit
slips) and the denominator always taken from the R twin, so every role is scaled by the physically correct
response. Targets: λR = 1; λD = λC = λK = 0. The certificate requires|y∗ R(zb) − y∗ R(za)| above the loosest
tolerance, so the denominator is never near zero; signs and zero golds need no logarithms.
4. Role-discrimination index Λ = λR − λD (target 1), a descriptive summary only: it is blind to some failures
(a model that answers correctly in R and subtracts the quantity in D hasλD = −1 and Λ = 2) and conflates
others (ignoring the quantity everywhere and using it everywhere both giveΛ = 0).
Multimodality guard. A location summary of a two-mode answer distribution can describe a smooth
response the model never produces (answers at 0 and 100 give a location near 50). Everyλr is therefore
reported with the cell’s answer-mode composition (shares of correct, each misuse mode, other and non-complete
answers); when two or more modes each hold at least 20% of the cell’s complete answers, λr is flagged
MULTIMODAL and not interpreted. Neither λ nor Λ is ever the sole basis of a claim about physical reasoning.
A cell with noCOMPLETE answers has nomr; the structure isNOT_EVALUATED for λ and Λ (it still counts for
tracking and answer-mode shares), and the share of such cells is reported by role. The earlier log-elasticity
formulation is withdrawn: it is undefined for zero or sign-changing golds and for mixed answer sets, and its
interaction is not sign-aligned across structures.
Misuse hypotheses as response curves. For each D, C or K cell the generator emits a prespecified set
of misuse functions fh(z) (copy the quantity; substitute it for the input of the same dimension; add it to a
sum of same-dimension terms; for C and K the most plausible wrong law or wrong regime that keeps it). A
misuse hypothesis is supported only when answers followfh(z) across several values ofz while controls do
not; a single answer equal tofh(z1) is not evidence of that misuse. The generator chooses values so that every
pair of misuse functions, and each misuse function and the certified response, differ by more than the loosest
tolerance at two or more of at least three values; pairs that cannot be separated are recorded as confounded
and not distinguished. Answer matching keepsall hypotheses an answer matches:UNIQUE_MATCH(h), MULTI_-
MATCH({h}), NO_MATCH; a reporting taxonomy may collapse these, but the overlap is always shown.
Diﬀiculty and wording controls. Value effects are estimated within role (diﬀiculty is roughly constant
across z inside a role); the relevant role’s no-cue diﬀiculty is recorded as a covariate. Every estimand is
estimated per phrasing.Agreement across phrasings, required before a role claim, means: the phrasing-by-role
interaction on each of the G4 contrasts F1–F3 (Section8) is inside its SESOI by two one-sided tests, or, where
that test is underpowered, each phrasing’s estimate exceeds the SESOI in the same direction; otherwise the
result is reported per phrasing and called wording-dependent.
F easibility .Not every structure admits every stratum. Infeasibility is recorded by the generator and never
imputed. A structure iscomplete for the primary contrast only if it has R and D cells at three values in two
phrasings, with |y∗ R(z) − y∗ D(z)| above the loosest tolerance and differing answer-token spans at every value.
Calibration gates countcomplete role-by-value structures, not structures in general (Section5.1).
Adapted problems. A counterfactual built on an external problem (PHYSICS, UGPhysics, PRISM-Physics
or any other source) is a new item: it needs its own certificate and validation; it does not inherit the source’s.
4.4 Supporting conditions
Kept from the October design and the Stage 14 cells, now subordinate to the role-by-value core: no cue;
style-matched non-numeric sentence; same-unit cue at three proximity levels kept asdistinct conditions (exact
match, nearwithinthegradingtolerance, tolerance-separated); incompatibleunitwiththesamedigits; numeric
metadata; convertible unit (the invariance/equivariance family, old Cue C); relevant edit of an existing input;
role reversal (use on request); formula hint (a positive diagnostic: expected to help or to do nothing, never
a gate); an explicit relevance instruction (“identify and ignore irrelevant information”); cue position (before

or after the relevant inputs); and a smallnon-physics dependency control (GSM-DC-style problems with the
same role manipulation) to tell a general numeric or dependency phenomenon from one that needs physical
semantics.

Rules. A record that is notCOMPLETE is never relabelled WRONG; it is “not correct” for O1 andUNKNOWN or
adjudicated for O2. Truncation requires evidence that the budget was exhausted; a missing end-of-thinking
marker alone isFORMAT_INVALID. Only text after the end-of-thinking marker is graded by the contract. Units
are converted with a dimension check, never stripped. Every record stores its relative error to the gold. Three
grading views are always reported: the declared last-printed-place rule (primary), the unit-convertible rule,
and relative error≤ 1% with dimension-checked conversion (the field convention of UGPhysics and PHYSICS).
Cells whose cue lies within a view’s tolerance of the gold stay in O1 and O2; they are flaggedsource-ambiguous
under that view and excluded only from claims about the source of the answer (copying versus computing).
A stratified parser audit reports the parser’s false-negative rate; no LLM judge enters a primary analysis. A
cell with zero evaluable records isNOT_EVALUATED, never a zero effect.
Retired: the legacy signed teacher-forced label (Slp, base 0, 0.5 nats) and any single-string teacher-forced
probability as an endpoint.Diagnostics only: the anchor-matched presence boost andRalt of Stage 14.
Sampling. Repeated samples per cell are required; greedy decoding gives one deterministic answer. The
Stage 14 reasoning runner for Qwen2.5 and Llama is greedy and unbatched, so a new contract version samples
at each model’s published defaults (recorded per record) and batches; Qwen3 thinking uses temperature 0.6,
top-p 0.95, top-k 20 as its model card requires. Greedy Stage 14 records are never pooled with sampled ones.

4.7 Hypotheses and their distinguishing predictions
All are legitimate outcomes; more than one can hold at once (numeric copying and a selection failure are not
exclusive). They refine the October families: H-N becomes H1 and H2, H-P becomes H3, H4 and H6, H-T is
the retired string construct plus the position and format controls, H-U is the convertible-unit family.

4.8 Causal identification standard
The withdrawn Phase-I paper failed because its intervention metric did not isolate the claimed function: a
knockout that raised the gold string on base and sensitive renderings alike was read as cue processing. Every
mechanism experiment therefore declares which of three claims it tests, and uses the metric of that claim.

Only T2 or T3, with the controls below and the role interaction defined next, can support a claim about a
physical-relevance computation; T1 supports a claim about answer readout only. Comparisons between an R
twin and a D twin, whose golds differ, are made only under T2 or T3, never by teacher-forcing one role’s trace
under the other role’s prompt (that trace would carry a physically wrong value). Candidate foils are fixed by
a prespecified physical error hypothesis, never chosen as the foil the model scores highest; a candidate pair
whose values lie within tolerance or share their answer-token span is T1-infeasible and recorded.
T wo interaction estimands. With ∆hmX = m(X,intervened) − m(X,clean) the effect of interventionh on
prompt X:
Ipresence = ∆ hmD − ∆hmN , I role = ∆ hmD − ∆hmR.
N is the token-aligned non-numeric sentence (so the intervened positions exist in both prompts; the no-cue
prompt cannot serve, since it has no tokens at the quantity’s position);R is the relevant-role twin with the
same numeral, unit and position at the same z. Ipresence can use any declared metric, sinceD and N share
a gold. Irole must use a behaviourally comparable outcome, because the two worlds have different certified
answers: tracking against each world’s own certified answer, or the answer-mode shares, under T3 (or T2 with
each world’s certified intermediate values); raw gold-string log-odds are never subtracted across worlds. The
clean effects beside each (m(D) − m(N ), m(D) − m(R)) are always reported. A component withIpresence ̸= 0
but Irole ≈ 0 is a numeral-cue component; a claim of physical-role routing requiresIrole ̸= 0, holding across
values and phrasings, with the controls below. A large equal effect on all prompts marks a general answer
component (the head-11 lesson).Ih elsewhere in this document meansIpresence or Irole as declared.
Protocol checklist (each item cites the source of the practice):
1. Noising (necessity) and denoising (suﬀiciency) both, reported separately; they are not complements
(Heimersheim and Nanda).
2. Counterfactuals in distribution: role-by-value minimal pairs that change only the role relation or only
the value, token-aligned; several corruptions per item; no Gaussian noise; zero ablation never as evidence
(Zhang and Nanda).
3. Logit difference or log-odds with each candidate shown; never probability; never normalised recovery (values
above one come from negative components, not cancellation).
4. Resample or interchange ablation from matched counterfactuals as primary, mean ablation as a sensitivity;
conclusions reported under both (Miller, Chughtai and Saunders; Li and Janson).
5. Direct and total effects, with a frozen-final-LayerNorm control for self-repair (Rushing and Nanda; McGrath
et al.).
6. Divergence check: patched activations against the natural distribution at the site, and KL on neutral
prompts (Grant et al.).
7. Attribution patching only as a screen; every reported component confirmed by exact patching (Kramár et
al.).
8. Selectionstabilityunderbootstrapsubsampling; discoveryandtestondisjointstructures(CertifiedCircuits;
review issue 6).
9. Matched random components as nulls; family-wise correction over the components tested.
Working research protocol – not completed results

######## PAGE 25 ########
PHYSMON | RESEARCH REDESIGN v2 (REVISED 11 NOV 2026) 25
10. Rescue begins within structure, value-matched (under T2 or T3): transfer the candidate state between
the R and D twins of one structure at the samez, where the principal difference is the role relation;
cross-structure donors with independent matching are a later, stronger generalisation test. A transfer must
change the computation as predicted while preserving unrelated information (value, unit, answer).
11. A variable claim needs causal abstraction: a role variable localised by DAS (pyvene) with interchange-
intervention accuracy on held-out pairs against neuron and random-subspace baselines (MIB), plus the
subspace-illusion check (Makelov et al.). A subspace from which role can be decoded is diagnostic; a
subspace whose interchange changes behaviour as predicted iscausally suﬀicient; only the second supports
a computation claim. Binding work shows several mechanisms can combine (Gur-Arieh, Geva and Geiger),
so a single isolated role feature is not assumed.
12. Reasoning models: T1 on a fixed trace, T3 with on-policy resampling (Thought Branches); never a hand-
edited trace as primary evidence; no conclusion from one sample.
13. Probes are diagnostic only (Hidden Error Awareness).
14. Held-out prediction: the sign and size of Ih on held-out structures, values and the second model are
committed before the test.
4.9 Claim hierarchy and evidence gates
The October claim levels are kept, with their content restated for the revised construct (they are written CL1–
CL6 here, to avoid confusion with stratum C, review checks C1–C10 and inventory items C01–C18; October
citations of “C1–C6” mean these levels).
• CL1 (benchmark): certified role strata and responses plus audited natural-language fidelity (B4), inde-
pendence, coverage and well-specified exclusions.
• CL2 (behavioural): a reproducible role-by-value pattern (O4) on unseen template clusters (G4), reported
across endpoints O1–O5 rather than one answer-string likelihood.
• CL3 (monitor, G7): correctly scoped single-input monitoring with paired incremental value beyond
deployable baselines and enough precision to resolve deployment trade-offs.
• CL4 (causal localisation): several valid intervention families identify specific components under T2 or
T3 with the interaction estimand, replicated on held-out structures and not explained by model damage.
• CL5 (mechanistic explanation): a falsifiable functional account with specific necessity, controlled suf-
ficiency, upstream/downstream path tests, causal abstraction and held-out prediction (Section4.8); gener-
alisation beyond the selection panel (G6).
• CL6 (repair, G7): a selective, generalising intervention that beats appropriate non-mechanistic alterna-
tives on a documented utility and cost frontier.
Promotion rule (kept). A claim advances one level only when the corresponding tests pass; a highly
significant CL3 monitor does not establish CL4 or CL5; a T1 readout result supports at most CL4 for readout.
The next paper needs either a convincing CL5, or an exceptionally well-validated CL1–CL2 finding with novelty
beyond the literature of Section11 (Track E), preferably with CL6 if feasible. “Shortcut reliance” is reserved
for evidence that the computation improperly uses the quantity (H3 or H4 established under T2 or T3). The
repository’s forbidden-phrase check stays on.

G2. Measurement and calibration (GPU, small)
1. Design-validation pilot (8–12 structures, core role-by-value cells, a few samples): are the contrasts
unambiguous, feasible, correctly certified and correctly graded? Structures are checked by the best available
reviewer (the qualified LLM panel once it exists, plus the user’s walkthrough; each labelled as such). Defects
found here change the generator, never the analysis of later data.
2. Calibration per candidate model and budget:ksel no-cue samples to select items, thenkest fresh samples
on the selected items to estimate the baseline and the self-flip floor (never the selection samples: the 14.20
preliminary contrast had a baseline of 1.000 by construction, J14.19-014); on a subset of the selected items,
a few samples of the R and D cells at three values in one phrasing and of the non-numeric sentence, so that
the variance of the actual primary estimands (tracking loss, misuse and neglect shares) is estimated, not
only a no-cue variance; tokens, budget exhaustion and format failures.
3. R-tracking check. A minimum tracking share on R cells, fixed numerically in G1, is checked here: a
model or budget below it does not use added relevant quantities reliably enough for any role reading, and
is changed or dropped at this gate, never after G3.
4. Primary-model rule, frozen at the end of G2 and before any G3 output: the primary model is the first
in the prespecified order Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Qwen3-8B (if downloaded, D3) that
meets the G2 criteria (complete structures in band, R-tracking criterion, extended parity in the study dtype
for G5 instrumentation); the next model that meets them is the second model. The choice never depends
on observed cue effects.
Gate G2. Passes when enough complete role-by-value structures (Section 4.3: R and D cells at three values in two
phrasings) fall in the band to meet the power target of Section 8 (planning: at least 24), the R-tracking check passes,
and the cost fits Section 9. Otherwise: add harder or easier variants or change the budget, and repeat G2; a model
that cannot be brought into the band is reported on the all-validated population only and its band-based discovery
is not run. The band and the R criterion are not changed after seeing G2 results.
G3. Behavioural discovery (GPU, staged)
1. Core run. 24–40 complete calibrated structures; core conditions: no cue; R and D roles at three values each
in two phrasings; the non-numeric sentence; plus the small non-physics dependency control set. Sampling
may be adaptive only by a rule fixed in G1. Results are reported on the calibrated population and, for the
same cells where run, on all validated structures.
2. T argeted explanatory ablations, added only when the core run shows something to explain: strata C
and K, marking and system membership, unit and proximity, position, relevance instruction, formula hint,
convertible units.
3. Hypothesis scorecard. For each of H0–H6 the prespecified evidence for and against (Section4.7) is
estimated with intervals and given one status: SUPPORTED, CONTRADICTED, INCONCLUSIVE or
NOT_EVALUATED. Several hypotheses may be supported at once; hypotheses are not exclusive rows and
are not read by first match. An interval that contains zero but is not inside the equivalence margin is
INCONCLUSIVE, never H0; H0 and H6 are SUPPORTED only by two one-sided tests, which G3’s size
usually cannot power, so in G3 they are normally INCONCLUSIVE. A null on the small non-physics control
is INCONCLUSIVE unless it is powered, and is not evidence of physics-specificity.
4. Optional exploratory mechanism pilot on the primary 7B model, if it helps discriminate hypotheses;
its results are never confirmatory and its site selection is separated from G5’s held-out tests.
Gate G3. The G4 question is fixed now, not chosen from G3’s largest estimate: G4 confirms the role-by-value family
(Section 8) whatever G3 shows, provided G2 passed. G3 can add at most one secondary family to G4, chosen by a
rule fixed in G1 and labelled as chosen on EXPLORATION data. If R tracking in G3 falls below the G1 criterion,
the G3 role result is reported as uninterpretable for role (itself a finding); items and band are not changed on the
same data. A formula hint that does not help is a diagnostic, not a gate.
G4. Independent behavioural confirmation (GPU, medium)
New structures in template clusters no earlier run has touched (INTERNAL_CONFIRMATION; shadow
subset held back), validated by the qualified LLM panel (Section3.7; human B4 review where available)
or, failing that, labelled EXPLORATORY-REPLICATION. Preregistered: the role-by-value family with its
estimands, decision rules and sample size from the power simulation; the primary and second models fixed by
the G2 primary-model rule, the second by fixed sequence; two declared final-answer formats on a random half
of items, each with its effect estimate and interval, and a stated rule for how much format dependence changes
the interpretation (planning: the reading changes if the format-specific effects differ by more than a factor of
two or have opposite signs with both intervals excluding zero). Opened once.

Gate G4. Passes when the primary family meets its rule on the primary model. If not, the G3 pattern is reported
as not replicated.
G5. Mechanism (GPU)
Gated on G4 establishing H3 or H4, or H6-RD (the mechanism of correct selection between relevant and struc-
turally disconnected quantities, when the model selects correctly and errors are rare; it needs the equivalence
tests that only G4’s size can power). A mechanism-of-correctness claim covers only the strata G4 confirmed:
H6-extended (C and K as well) needs those strata in G4’s preregistered family; under H1/H2 only a narrow
study of unit or number handling, framed against Liu and Owusu et al. The exploratory mechanism pilot of
G3 is the only mechanism work before G4. Every experiment declares claim type T1, T2 or T3 and follows Sec-
tion 4.8. Starts on the primary and second models fixed by the G2 rule (planning order Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct,
Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct; both listed as fully verified by TransformerLens 3.4; locally, HF-versus-TL parity has
passed only on one smoke prompt in float16 with parameters on CPU, job 399217, so the G0 extended parity
in the study dtype is required first); Qwen3-8B with thinking afterwards (if downloaded, D3); Qwen3-32B only
for a frozen-function transfer test.
Gate G5. A role-computation claim needs T2 or T3 evidence with Irole ̸= 0 (not only Ipresence), both directions,
rescue within structure, causal abstraction for any variable claim, and a correct held-out prediction. Otherwise the
result is reported at the level it reached (Section 4.9).
G6. External and functional confirmation
Independently sourced physics problems (EPC; adaptations of PHYSICS, UGPhysics or PRISM-Physics where
feasible, each re-certified and re-validated as a new item); non-physics transfer (GSM-DC or GSM-Symbolic
NoOp with the same role-by-value logic where it maps); a second model family; frozen function, not frozen
component index. Required for any broad generalisation claim.
G7. Practical use (optional)
Monitoring (the Phase-I monitor under cluster-held-out folds is a side track, D6) and selective repair against
a cheap ladder (relevance instruction, self-consistency, longer budget), with strength-versus-damage curves.
5.2 The original critical-path blocks P0–P11 under the revised gates
The October edition ordered its work as twelve critical-path blocks, P0 to P11. They are kept here, with
their identifiers, questions, sub-items, hard gates and failure responses, because they remain the most detailed
statement of what each kind of evidence requires. They no longer set the order of execution: that is fixed
by the gates G0–G7 (Section5.1), and the construct, strata, endpoints, hypotheses and causal standard are
those of Section4. Where a block’s text conflicts with either, Sections4 and 5.1 win; the conflicts known at
this revision are resolved in the block text below and listed in itsDisposition line. Block text that names the
legacy constructs (Slp, Cue A/B/C, the four-rendering family, L16 H11) is rewritten in terms of the role strata
R/D/C/K, the role-by-value design and the outcomes O1–O6 wherever the requirement survives.
Three rules of the October dependency paragraph stay in force. (1) Each gate is about correctness, not
dates; the plan is not calendar-driven. (2) A claim ledger is updated continuously (P11) but final claims are
frozen only when the branches they need have closed. (3) Mechanism work does not start before trustworthy
partitions and a frozen behavioural contrast exist; in the revised plan that means after G4, for H3, H4 or
H6-RD (Section5.1). The October allowance for “exploratory H11 checks” is replaced by a narrower one: a
small exploratory mechanistic pilot may run during G3, marked exploratory and never confirmatory, and no
claim may rest on it.

5.2.1 P0. Independent evidence reproduction, release provenance and code audit
Question (October). Which of Phase I’s reported numbers follow from the exact datasets, versions, model
weights and scoring code? A corrupted label, leaked fold or misaligned hook invalidates downstream mecha-
nistic interpretation.
Revised scope (G0). The Phase-I paper was withdrawn on 11 November 2026, and no new claim rests on
its numbers. Full bottom-up regeneration of Phase-I values is therefore off the critical path (open decision
D1); if the full P0 is kept, it runs as a side track and blocks none of G1–G4. What remains on the critical path
is the part that protectsnew evidence: hooks that touch the tensors and positions they claim, and registers
that tie every number to bytes.
P0.1 Immutable artifact and claim registry (kept).
Every family or structure instance gets an identifier; hashes are frozen for the symbolic template, rendered
text, response prefix, reference answer, model revision, tokenizer, generation configuration, scoring script,
fold, intervention site, donor and target identities, scheduler job, git SHA and seed. A machine-readable
map links each claim_id to artifact paths, generator code, checksum, eligibility rule and source table or
figure, and marks exploration, internal confirmation and untouched confirmation. Missing, cancelled and
zero-row runs are registered.
P0.2 Bottom-up reproduction of the submission tables (off the critical path).
Regenerating the 155 → 140 → 135 inclusion flow, per-cue rates, label overlaps, AUROC/AUPRC, Brier,
ECE, FNR@FPR, out-of-fold predictions, bootstrap distributions, the layer-16 head ranking, causal per-
family numerators and denominators and the 15-family transfer membership[SUBMITTED] is part of the
D1 side track only.
P0.3 End-to-end re-run (narrowed).
Two pieces stay. (a)Extended parity: Hugging Face against TransformerLens at the hook sites G5 will use,
on traces of the planned length, for every model that enters mechanism work. (b) A forward-pass spot
check of 10 legacy families’ stored log-probabilities, stratified as in October (includingCM_B_UM_059 and
the adversarial edge cases), runonly if a Phase-I number is cited again.
P0.4 Leakage and cohort-selection code inspection (rules carried forward).
The Phase-I code audit belongs to the side track. Its rules apply to all new work: scalers, features,

P0.5 Provenance discrepancies (logged, not resolved).
The renamed-donor control (zero evaluable rows in the manuscript, “completed with zero recovery” in an

5.2.2 P1. Measurement validity: challenge the entire sensitivity construct
Question (October). Does the observed signal reflect improper computation by the model, or mainly a
property of the string and the scoring interface?
Revised scope (G0, G2). The question has been answered for the legacy construct well enough to retire
it (Section4.5): Slp and any single-string teacher-forced probability are no longer endpoints, and the anchor-
matched presence boost and Ralt are diagnostics only. P1’s sub-items therefore survive in two forms: as
completed Stage 14 evidence, and as measurement checks that G2 applies to the new contract (noise floor,
format robustness, parse rates).
P1.1 Anchor-free rescoring and base permutation.
Done for the legacy label (X02). No further work.
P1.2 No-cue and non-numeric controls.
Cue absent, irrelevant numeric distractor, style-matched non-numeric sentence, numeric metadata and a
re-certified relevant edit, compared as matched differences-in-differences. These are now standing conditions
of the design (Section4.4).
P1.3 Output-wrapper multiverse.
Done on the v2 structures under seven wrappers. Carried forward: exact tokenizer IDs for every scored
sequence and prefix, no prompt or padding tokens in a scored span, and the two declared final-answer
formats that G4 runs.
P1.4 Length and tokenization.
Tokenizer audit done. Open, optional: first-token versus full-sequence scores and value-only versus value-
plus-unit likelihood (computable from stored per-token log-probabilities).
P1.5 Proper likelihood comparisons.
Correct-versus-decoy log-odds measured as anchor-matched answer competition; now a diagnostic. Within
a mechanism claim the candidate pair is the one fixed by Section4.8, never the foil the model scores highest.
P1.6 F ree generation.
Done with reasoning (Stages 14.13, 14.15, 14.19–14.20). The October requirement of repeated stochas-
tic samples per cell is now part of the contract (Section4.5); the transition categories (correct→wrong,
wrong→different wrong, invalid) survive inside O1–O3.
P1.7 Metric reliability .
Done for dtype (bfloat16 reproducible; noise SD 0.09–0.19 nats). Carried forward: G2 estimates each
model’s own sampling and self-flip floor on fresh samples.
P1.8 Selective prediction.
Open, optional: confidence bins for final-answer correctness, ECE/Brier with cluster intervals, stable versus
