Gate P1 (October), resolved. The October branches have been taken: the legacy Slp is not called a shortcut
construct; Cue C is separated as the convertible-unit (invariance/equivariance) family; and the thesis moved from
likelihood sensitivity to the role-by-value response in free generation (O4). Any new likelihood finding is reported as
a diagnostic and carries no safety or correctness claim on its own.
Status (11 Nov 2026): largely done in Stage 14, all exploratory. X02: 40–49% (Qwen) and 41–56%
(Llama) of base-0 positives flip with the choice of base. Stage 14.10: the sign of the cue effect persists in all
seven wrappers, its size depends on format for Qwen, and parse rates depend heavily on format. Stages 14.14
and 14.17: every number in a prompt receives an answer-presence boost, a cue more than a relevant input;
plausibility matching removes about half of the same-unit cue effect, and the remainder depends on unit
compatibility. Open and optional: P1.4 value-only and first-token scores, P1.8 selective prediction. The
cross-instruction stability check of any label on the pilot families is a G0 item (Section5.1).
5.2.3 P2. Scale the approved DECOY-v2 design (not the old benchmark)
Question (October). Can the proposed mechanism’s causal ingredients be manipulated independently while
preserving physics, with genuinely new structures held out?
Revised scope (G1, feeding G3 and G4). Scale-up is demoted: P2 builds only the structures G3 and
G4 need, in the counts the gates fix (Section5.1). The October range of 300–600 new canonical structures
[PROPOSAL] is withdrawn as a target. The generator requirements stay, re-expressed in the role-by-value
design.
P2.1 Explicit generative grammar.
Typed quantities, dimensions, roles and assumptions; the equation as a directed computation graph from
inputs through intermediates to the target. Each quantity carries the certificate of its stratum (R, D, C or
K; Section4.2), and an independent semantic checklist verifies that the rendered text matches the graph.
Negative-control structures with a planted coupling must be rejected by the validators. Free-symbol absence
alone is not a certificate when the omitted quantity changes assumptions, frames or boundary conditions.
P2.2 F actorial design (recast).
The October six axes map onto the design of Sections4.3 and 4.4: physical status becomes the role strata;
numerical closeness becomes the three proximity levels kept as distinct conditions, plus valuesz1, . . . , zm
for the dependency curve; units become same-unit, incompatible-unit-same-digits and convertible-unit cells;
semantic relationship becomes at least two validated phrasings per role relation, one without marker words;
placement becomes the cue-position condition; task structure becomes the diﬀiculty variants. Fractional or
blocked designs are prespecified, never chosen after outcomes.
P2.3 Crucial deconfounding cells (kept).
Equal cue digits with different physical role; equal role with different digit overlap; matched answer value
under a different law; same law at a different instantiation; same numeral and unit with a different role
phrasing. The role-by-value cells provide most of these by construction.
P2.4 Quantity and independence (kept, target withdrawn).
Count distinct computation graphs, not paraphrases. Complete template clusters, law combinations and
source collections are reserved for confirmation. If there are too few genuinely different graphs, prefer fewer
valid structures and a narrower stated scope.
P2.5 Domain extension.
Each new domain is a separate cohort, not pooled into a favourable aggregate; domain diﬀiculty is a
measured covariate.
P2.6 Out-of-distribution sources.
Moved to G6 (external sets, below under P11). Adapted external problems are new items and need their
own certificates (Section4.3).
P2.7 Adversarially plausible wording.
Independent LLMs may flag ambiguity and suggest tricky distractors but never assign physics ground
truth; admission requires rewriting and symbolic validation; rejection reasons and excluded structures are
published.
P2.8 Matched negative and positive sets.
Now the supporting conditions of Section4.4, including role reversal (use on request), which separates a
selective relevance computation from indiscriminate digit suppression.
P2.9 Domain-specific robustness.
Dimension conversions, significant-figure conventions, sign and frame conventions, rounding, near-zero de-
nominators and degenerate limits are checked; any tacit real-world assumption gets a stated-assumption

5.2.4 P3. Independent expert validation, parser reliability and leakage firewall
Question. Is every confirmatory item’s natural language correct, is every graded answer read correctly, and
is no confirmation structure related to anything used in discovery? A positive model result never waives these
requirements. Kept in full; mapped to G1 (rules and mutation tests frozen), G2 (parser audit on the new
contract) and G4 (validation of confirmation structures, cohort freeze).
P3.1 Personnel and blinding.
Two independent physics-qualified validators per confirmatory structure and a third adjudicator (interim:
the qualified LLM panel of Section3.7, under the same blinding), calibrated on easy, adversarial and am-
biguous cases, blind to model outputs, scores and the hypothesis. Each property asked separately: equation
correctness, suﬀicient assumptions, the role certificate of each quantity (Section4.2), answer invariance or
certified response, naturalness, missing interactions, units, rounding, and whether paired renderings differ
only as intended. Confidence and reasons are recorded.
P3.2 Disagreement.
Predefined exclusion and adjudication rules; raw agreement, Cohen’sκ and a prevalence-aware alterna-
tive under imbalance, structure-level bootstrap intervals, domain failure rates and adjudication edits and
changed-label counts. The October aspiration ofκ = 0.80 stays an aspiration, never a licence to drop hard
cases.
P3.3 Mutational verification.
Deliberate failure mutations (quantity leaks into the equation, changed assumption, removed isolation,
unit error, sign flip, changed relevant variable, renamed role, swapped target, hidden dependence, missing
boundary condition) and algebraically equivalent positive mutations; sensitivity and specificity by mutator;
invalid items must fail for the intended reason. For strata C and K the mutations include breaking the
cancellation and leaving the regime.
P3.4 Parser study .
A blinded, stratified sample across models, conditions and formats, including refusals, multiple numbers,
intermediate answers, hallucinated units, LaTeX-wrapped final lines, scientific notation, significant figures,
symbolic answers and truncations; two human adjudicators; coverage, error rate, coverage conditional on
outcome, answer-equivalence false positives, and conservative bounds on behavioural rates. The O3 status
categories (COMPLETE, BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, FORMAT_INVALID, UNPARSEABLE, MULTIPLE_CANDIDATES, EMPTY)
are audited as categories in their own right; ambiguous responses stay explicit. The audit reports the
parser’s false-negative rate; no LLM judge enters a primary analysis.
P3.5 Multi-level overlap detection.
Union-find clusters over prompt hashes, number-masked text, symbolic AST, equation-graph isomorphism,
governing law, frame, renamed graph, cue grammar, near-duplicate embeddings, reviewed semantic relations
and identical solution programs; a frozen clustering policy with a manually adjudicated sample; transitive
siblings never straddle splits. Same law is held out in a stricter transfer test.
P3.6 Audit of the original 34 clusters.
Review of the 2,352 unresolved rendering pairs and 147 family pairs, and re-evaluation of the original
LOOCV by cluster-held-out and by distinct symbolic program, is needed only if v1 families are reused.
Always required: a report of overlap between v1 and v2 structures and every new locked confirmation set
(G4, G6); newly generated paraphrases of old computation graphs stay in discovery.
P3.7 Cohort freeze.
Discovery, internal confirmation, EPC confirmation, adversarial challenge, the human-written source set and
the shadow set are manifested, and every structure and variant gets an immutable split before any outcome
Working research protocol – not completed results

######## PAGE 33 ########
PHYSMON | RESEARCH REDESIGN v2 (REVISED 11 NOV 2026) 33
is seen; a removed structure keeps a tombstone with its reason; intent-to-evaluate is reported beside eligible
results. A structure never moves from EXPLORATION into a confirmation role.
Gate P3. No confirmatory behavioural, hidden-state or causal generalisation claim until each confirmatory structure’s
natural language has passed independent validation and its leakage risk is audited. If the certificate proves the
equations but validators reject a sizeable share of the prompts’ semantics, revise the benchmark and restart the
affected measurements; this is not a statistical nuisance covariate. Until human review exists, independent validation
for G4 is provided by the qualified LLM panel of Section 3.7, disclosed as such; without a qualified panel, G4 runs as
EXPLORATORY-REPLICATION and no text may call it confirmatory.

5.2.5 P4. Definitive behavioural discrimination and power planning
Question. Which of H0–H6 (Section4.7) describes the model’s behaviour on certified role-by-value structures,
and with what precision? P4 is now the scientific centre of the plan: its exploratory half is G3 and its
preregistered half is G4.
P4.1 A small preregistered core experiment (recast).
The October primary contrast (proximity × unit compatibility × relevance on answer contamination,
correct-versus-decoy log-odds and likelihood dispersion) is replaced by the role-by-value interaction on O4
(Section 4.3), with O1, O2, O3 and O5 reported beside it; proximity, unit and marking are moderators.
G4 preregisters the role-by-value family fixed in advance (Section5.1), with its estimands, decision rules
and sample size, on held-out structures in untouched clusters, and opens it once; G3 may add at most one
secondary family, labelled as chosen on EXPLORATION data. Broad multiverse tables are secondary.
P4.2 Honest power.
Simulation from discovery-only data with cluster dependence and within-structure correlation, including
the variance of a cue difference, not only the no-cue variance; sample size for the smallest scientifically
meaningful effect; attrition from parser and validator failures recorded; a precision-limited conclusion when
the interval cannot be narrowed.
P4.3 Multi-level models.
Structure random intercepts and, where estimable, random slopes, or predeclared cluster-robust models;
only predeclared interactions (role× value, role × marking, proximity × digit overlap, unit compatibility,
position, model); family-wise or FDR control over any wider scan, with confirmation.
P4.4 Near-match profile (kept).
The Phase-I Pearson 0.074[SUBMITTED] is a warning. Monotone distance, threshold or tail, and token-
overlap models are compared by out-of-cluster predictive density; counterexamples to each (close but digit-
disjoint, digit-similar but far, exact value with incompatible units). Misuse hypotheses are tested as response
curves over several values ofz, never from a single matching answer.
P4.5 Same panel across models.
Identical certified items on every compared model, chosen inside every configuration’s calibration band
(Section 4.6); thinking on versus off within the same weights answers the secondary question; exact model
revisions and chat templates are recorded.
P4.6 Severity and validity strata.
Positive-structure rate, median and tail effects, answer changes, correctness transitions, high-confidence
errors, O3 statuses and token cost reported separately; effects must survive dropping the one to three most
extreme structures; means and robust quantiles both reported.
P4.7 Core negative tests (kept, restated).
If the departure is reproduced by an irrelevant bibliographic numeral, is unchanged by unit incompatibility,
does not differ between role twins, vanishes under equivalent output formats, or tracks only token overlap,
the evidence counts against H3 and for H1 or H2 in the scorecard (hypotheses are not exclusive, Section5.1);
H6-RD is supported only when F1–F3 (D and R) are each shown equivalent to zero; H6-extended adds C
and K. These are results, not failures to hide; a certified null is reported with its power.
Working research protocol – not completed results

######## PAGE 34 ########
PHYSMON | RESEARCH REDESIGN v2 (REVISED 11 NOV 2026) 34
Gate P4 (now G3 then G4). Mechanism work proceeds only after the role-by-value family has passed G4
(Section 5.1); the contrast fixes the claim type and metric of Section 4.8, and the legacy normalised recovery is never
reused. If the only effect is format-sensitive confidence drift or cost (H5), report it as such. If strata or conditions
behave differently, choose one primary contrast for mechanism and treat the others as explicit scope tests. A cell with
zero evaluable records is NOT_EVALUATED, never a zero effect.
Status (11 Nov 2026): G3 and G4 not started; G1 (construct freeze) comes first. The Stage 14 pilots
predate the role-by-value design and contain no matched role twins. The Stage 14.20 cue cells on 32 Qwen3-
32B candidate anchors (job 435605, one sample per cell) gave 2 wrong and 17 not evaluated of 128 cells; the
sampling-noise baseline (job 435606) was cancelled on the user’s instruction before it started, so the cue-effect
contrast isNOT_EVALUATED; the preliminary analysis is selection-biased by construction and read descriptively
only. Its most informative signal is length (role-reversal cells about 45% more tokens than the no-cue anchors).
5.2.6 P5. A definitive monitoring study: does access to hidden states help?
Thesis (kept). A monitor is an operational advance only if it is deployable under its claimed input budget,
calibrated for its target, statistically and practically better than cheaper alternatives on unseen structures, and
robust to shift. A predictor that reads four renderings is a counterfactual-family diagnostic, not a one-input
detector.
Revised scope (G7). Demoted to an optional side track: the primary question no longer needs a monitor.
The monitored target must be a frozen endpoint of Section4.5, not the retiredSlp. Every comparator carries
an oracle or deployable tag stating what it needs at inference (in particular, whether it uses the gold answer);
no comparator built from the label’s own inputs is called “non-activation” or “one forward pass”.
P5.1 Three separate tasks.
S (single prompt, no other family member at inference), F (full family, compared with a multi-query
behavioural measurement), V (variant-local, per-variant labels); no pooled AUROC across them.
P5.2 Three frozen feature sets.
One predeclared residual layer from discovery, the embedding layer as lexical control, next-token log-
its/entropy as cost-matched comparator; other sites are discovery scans.
P5.3 Comparator ladder.
Constant and base-rate predictors; prompt-only text features; frozen-encoder embeddings; one-pass output
uncertainty; generic correctness and semantic-entropy predictors; black-box multi-query consistency with
real pass counts; post-generation critics (not pre-generation competitors); a fully tuned non-activation stack.
Each with its oracle/deployable tag.
P5.4–P5.6 Probe capacity , generalisation level, leakage controls.
Capacity-matched probe families with random-label controls; prediction across instantiations, clusters, laws,
conditions and checkpoints (a signal that needs the same scaffold in training is template recognition);
permuted-label and irrelevant-metadata controls.
P5.7–P5.9 Deconfounding, selection accounting, calibration.
Incremental value over correctness and entropy by nested stacking and paired loss on the external set; layer
chosen on discovery and frozen; calibrators fitted on development groups only; FNR at FPR 0.05 and 0.10
[PROPOSAL] with full curves and intervals; prevalence shift evaluated separately.
P5.10–P5.11 Information bounds and cost.
Oracle features are non-deployable upper bounds; wall-clock, memory and throughput per decision on the
same hardware.
Gate P5 (kept). A monitor is promoted only if a frozen single-input specification shows a practically meaningful,
statistically supported incremental advantage on a held-out structural cohort under a preregistered endpoint. Oth-
erwise monitorability is a descriptive diagnostic and the null incremental value is reported. An AUROC above 0.5 is
not incremental value.
Status (11 Nov 2026): sidetrack, notscheduled(opendecisionD6). ThePhase-Imonitorundercluster-held-
out folds isNOT_EVALUATED: its activation tensors were lost and must be regenerated. Known from committed
files: against the oracle-free entropy baseline (0.520) the paper’s comparator (0.727, fitted on the label’s own
inputs) [SUBMITTED] was oracle-like; the same applies to the Wave 2 comparator. The oracle/deployable
tag and its propagation to the Wave 2 record and the claim ledger are G0 items.
5.2.7 P6. Re-localise the phenomenon under valid causal metrics and selection rules
Question (revised). Which components, if any, have an effect on the role-by-value contrast that passed G4
— an interactionIh ̸= 0 under the declared claim type (T1, T2 or T3; Section4.8) — rather than a general
Working research protocol – not completed results

######## PAGE 35 ########
PHYSMON | RESEARCH REDESIGN v2 (REVISED 11 NOV 2026) 35
effect on the answer?
Retired as stated: the H11 lesion (card X07). The October question asked whether Qwen layer-16
head 11 is a causal component. The Phase-I evidence does not support starting there: the four-head L16
knockout inverted the signed drop (normalised recovery above one) in 17 of 20 families, mean recovery 1.87,
and removing head 11 alone raised the certified answer’s first-token logit by 3.76 on base and 3.77 on sensitive
renderings, in 20 of 20 families each[SUBMITTED], verified from the released files. An effect equal on both
prompts marks a general answer component. Components are found anew under the interaction estimand; the
legacy L16 sites, and the Llama L21 H2 candidate, have no privileged status.
P6.1 Pairs chosen prospectively .
The counterfactuals are the role-by-value minimal pairs (R and D twins of one structure at the samez; the
same role at two values), token-aligned, several per item, labelled by design and not by observed sensitivity;
stratified by correctness and by O3 status. Where alignment is impossible, only semantically matched
positions are patched, with position controls. Selection on a discovery split; tests on disjoint held-out
structures.
P6.2 F rozen response variable.
The metric of the declared claim type (Section4.8): T1 logp(y∗(z)) −log p(fh(z)) on the declared prefix,
between prompts that share a gold, each candidate’s logit shown; T2 the certified intermediate against the
prespecified misuse value; T3 O1, O2 and O4 over on-policy resampled traces. Original score, intervened
score and absolute difference are always reported, forD, N and (under T2/T3) R, with the clean effects
beside Ipresence and Irole; never a normalised recovery and never a ratio over near-zero denominators.
P6.3 A new experiment, not a reproduction.
Candidates come from a discovery screen on EXPLORATION structures, with flanking layers, norm- and
entropy-matched heads and random sites as controls; per-structure before/after values reported.
P6.4 Several ablation semantics.
Resample or interchange ablation from matched counterfactuals as primary, mean ablation as sensitivity,
the conclusion stated under both; projection removal and rescaling as further sensitivities; zero ablation
never as evidence. A method-by-site stability table, not one intervention flavour.
P6.5 Specific necessity .
Noising a component must change the role-specific effect while preserving, within a preregistered tolerance,
the response to relevant inputs (the R twin’s certified response), unrelated problems and role reversal. No
global claim of logical necessity: redundant pathways are expected.
P6.6 Suﬀiciency with the right variables.
Denoising and transfer begin within structure, value-matched, between the R and D twins; cross-structure
donors come later. Dose sweeps in both directions; effects on generated answers, not only on logits; content-
preserving swaps from same-answer, same-law and same-unit irrelevant donors. An injection that changes
a likelihood score but not answers or the certified-versus-misuse competition is not called suﬀiciency.
P6.7 Off-target damage and self-repair.
An independent control suite (no-cue physics, relevant edits, unrelated numeric and lexical tasks, common
natural-language QA and syntactic completion); loss and KL shifts on neutral prompts, next-token entropy
and output length; compensatory changes in nearby heads and MLPs; local replacement against global
ablation; divergence of patched activations from the natural distribution; direct and total effects with a
frozen-final-LayerNorm control.
P6.8 Second model.
Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct is localised afresh on its own discovery split; a site that misses triggers a discovery
sweep on exploratory data, never repeated scans of confirmation structures. Reasoning models follow the
T1/T3 split of Section 4.8. October’s DeepSeek requirement (confirm the prompt boundary, reasoning
trace and final-answer scoring, and match denominators, before concluding that a reasoning model lacks a
pathway) applies to any reasoning model studied; DeepSeek-R1-Distill itself is not planned (AppendixC).
Gate P6 (part of G5). A component advances to P7 as a role component only if Irole ̸= 0 under T2 or T3 with
the controls of Section 4.8, robust across ablation semantics, on held-out structures; with Ipresence ̸= 0 alone it is a
numeral-cue component. An effect equal on D, N and R marks a general answer component and is reported as such.
An effect shown only under T1 supports a readout claim, not a role-computation claim. An effect on log-odds but
not on O1, O2 or O4 is a cause of answer-competition change, not of success or failure in physics.
Status (11 Nov 2026): not started; gated on G4. No activations exist for the v2 items. Parity for the two
7–8B models is in hand (P0); extended parity is not.
Working research protocol – not completed results

5.2.8 P7. Identify what the causal components compute
Question. What function connects the quantity’s tokens to the model’s dependence, or independence, of its
answer on that quantity? Localisation without function is not a mechanism claim.
P7.1 Anatomy of each surviving component.
(Was: head 11 at L16.) For every relevant position (inputs, the quantity’s value and unit, the role phrasing,
the question, the last prompt position, answer positions): attention logits and patterns, output norm, OV
contribution and direct attribution across the role-by-value pairs. Attention maps are not causal evidence;
attention probabilities and value vectors are patched separately.
P7.2 Candidate functions tested head-to-head (kept), mapped to the revised hypotheses. •
F-copy (retrieves or copies a distractor numeral) andF-answer prior (shifts one output format or length
without representing the quantity)→ H1;
• F-match (equality or proximity of numeral and target) andF-unit (dimension or unit matching)→ H2;
• F-role (semantic disconnection or role relation suppresses an attractive candidate)→ H3;
• F-position (near-query tokens or sentence order)→ the cue-position control;
• added: readout (correct value computed in the trace, final answer moved toward the quantity)→ H4,
tested under T1 at answer positions on a fixed trace;
• added: correct selection (D, C, K invariant and R correct)→ H6, whose mechanism is studied when
errors are rare.
Each function needs at least two interventions whose predictions differ from the alternatives: same digits
with an incompatible unit (F-copy yes, F-unit no); same magnitude, digit-disjoint form (F-match yes, F-
copy no); same tokens moved (F-position changes, F-match preserved); the R twin or role reversal (F-role
reverses, F-copy need not). These are cells of Sections4.3 and 4.4, evaluated on a held-out grid, not on
anecdotes.
P7.3 Activation decoding with interventions.
Nested linear probes for the numeral, target magnitude, digit overlap, unit compatibility, role and relevant
inputs are diagnostic only; subspace interventions that remove one decoded variable while preserving others
test behaviour; causal directions are classified as independent, oblique or redundant. A decodable subspace
is diagnostic; only a subspace whose interchange changes behaviour as predicted is causally suﬀicient.
P7.4 Representation geometry .
Matched differences ∆(z1, z2) and ∆(R,D) at key sites; cross-structure alignment (CKA, CCA, principal
angles, projection energy) against equal-dimension random and nearest-neighbour nulls; subspaces fitted on
discovery only and used to predict held-out causal effects.
P7.5 Direct logit attribution.
On the prespecified candidate pair only, followed by exact counterfactual patching; decomposed into own-
role candidate, other-role candidate, both, or generic length.
P7.6 T emporal localisation.
Now expressed through the claim types: T2 on a teacher-forced prefix up to the step where the quantity
enters (for C and K intermediate use is expected, not penalised); T1 at answer positions on a fixed trace; free
explanations aligned only by semantic events and descriptive unless resampling makes positions comparable.
P7.7 Invariance and role reversal.
The proposed representation is patched between the R and D twins at the samez; both the normal and the
role-reversed response are predicted. A transfer must change the computation as predicted while preserving
value, unit and unrelated answer content.
P7.8 Hypothesis scorecard.
For each function: predeclared sign predictions over the cells, held-out prediction score (sign and size of
Ih committed before the test), selective patch effect, falsifying control, the alternative it beats, and failure
cases. The simplest function that explains held-out intervention effects is preferred.
Gate P7 (part of G5). Advance only if at least one explicit functional hypothesis predicts effect direction across
independent manipulations and survives direct causal tests under T2 or T3. Otherwise report a localised but un-
interpreted causal handle, try larger multi-component representations (P8), or pivot to Track E (the behavioural
and measurement result). No activation feature is called “physics-relevance” because its top examples sound physics-
related.
Status (11 Nov 2026): not started; gated on P6. Under H1 or H2 after G3, only the optional unit-matching
study is in scope, framed against the closest prior accounts (Section4.1).
Working research protocol – not completed results

######## PAGE 37 ########
PHYSMON | RESEARCH REDESIGN v2 (REVISED 11 NOV 2026) 37
5.2.9 P8. Recover and validate upstream and downstream computation, not one head
Question. Which source-to-mediator-to-sink path carries the role information, and does an explicit high-level
algorithm agree with the network under interchange? Kept; gated on G4 and on P6/P7.
P8.1 Sources and sinks declared first.
Sources: the quantity’s value and unit tokens, the role phrasing, relevant inputs, law words, the format
instruction. Sinks: mediators that passed P6/P7 and the metric of the declared claim type. Contrasts: the
R/D twins at the samez (primary) and two values within a role; proximity contrasts as moderators.
P8.2 T wo discovery procedures.
Attribution patching (with integrated-gradient refinement where it saturates) as a ranking screen, plus
targeted activation patching; optional mask optimisation. Every reported component is confirmed by exact
patching.
P8.3 Path patching.
Receiver-conditioned path patching for source to mediator, mediator to downstream and downstream to
answer, with checks of hook order, graph direction, tolerance and reverse interventions; the path must
matter only when the mediator receives the source information.
P8.4 Knockout–rescue ordering.
Knock out the source and measure the loss; rescue with the mediator’s clean activation; knock out the
mediator and predict that upstream rescue fails; control with unrelated and same-answer donors; rescue a
role-reversed task to show the path is not a destructive filter; contrast against rescuing a generic next-token
loss change.
P8.5 Completeness and minimality .
Model run with only the hypothesised edges against matched replacement of the complement; suﬀiciency,
comprehensiveness, selectivity, stability over corruptions; effect-versus-size and specificity-versus-size curves
in absolute metric units with each candidate shown; random matched graphs and a whole-residual patch as
baselines; residual unexplained effect reported.
P8.6 Causal abstraction.
An explicit high-level algorithm (e.g. parse inputs, parse candidate values, evaluate role and unit, choose
the answer) with a map from neural subspaces to its variables; a role variable localised by DAS with
interchange-intervention accuracy on held-out pairs against neuron and random-subspace baselines, plus the
subspace-illusion check (Section4.8). One high-level variable is varied at a time while correlated variables
are held fixed. Poor interchange agreement falsifies the account whatever the knockout sizes.
P8.7 Bottleneck hypotheses.
Does the mediator store the raw value, normalised magnitude, a role flag, a source identifier or a merged
candidate; does it act as a routing gate or a logit amplifier; confirmed on held-out laws, magnitudes, prompts
and positions. Several binding mechanisms may combine; one isolated role feature is not assumed.
P8.8 Sparse features (optional).
SAEs, transcoders, DAS and neurons compared at equal compute and feature budget; reconstruction error,
seed stability and causal interchange evaluated; SAEs are a method under test.
P8.9 Synthetic ground truth.
A small model trained with a planted numeric rule, and a matched model without it, tests whether the
pipeline recovers a known route; recovering it does not prove the same route operates naturally in the
studied models, but failure to recover it questions the method.
Gate P8 (part of G5). A mechanism claim needs a compact algorithmic account with validated source-to-mediator-
to-sink effects on untouched structures and held-out predictions that a simpler lexical or generic alternative cannot
explain (the mechanism rung of Section 4.9). Redundant routes are reported as a distributed or partially redundant
mechanism, not forced into a single-head story. If only correlational graphs emerge, conclusions stop at localisation.
Status (11 Nov 2026): not started; gated on G4.
5.2.10 P9. Cross-model, cross-domain and post-training generalisation
Question. Does the identified function recur beyond the discovery model, domain and format? Kept; gated
on G4 and on a frozen function from P7/P8. The within-model replication is part of G5; external and cross-
domain confirmation is G6.
P9.1 Cross-architecture confirmation.
Freeze the function, not the head index. Fresh discovery samples localise functional analogues in the second
architecture; the hypothesis is evaluated on untouched clusters with the same claim type and metric. A
functional analogue in a different head is replication; a failed matched-layer knockout is not a complete null.
Working research protocol – not completed results

######## PAGE 38 ########
PHYSMON | RESEARCH REDESIGN v2 (REVISED 11 NOV 2026) 38
P9.2 Scaling ladder.
Conditional on compute, small to large within one family; behaviour across scale before expensive causal
cases; only models with parity-tested hooks and answer scoring. In this plan Qwen3-32B enters only for a
frozen-function transfer test.
P9.3 Same-backbone post-training.
Base, instruct and reasoning variants with prompting controlled; thinking on versus off within the same
weights. Differences are not attributed to RL unless comparable training runs isolate it.
P9.4 F amiliar-to-novel-law transfer.
Valid symbolic worlds or dimensionally coherent toy laws with explicit rules and diﬀiculty matched by
solver-assistedpilots; togetherwiththenon-physicsdependencycontrol(Section 4.4)thisseparatesageneral
numeric or dependency phenomenon from one that needs physical semantics.
P9.5 Source and language transfer.
Human-written problems, new formats, terse equations, narratives and validated bilingual renderings;
English-only results do not imply cross-lingual generality.
P9.6 Composition and adversarial boundary .
Two or three simultaneous quantities of different roles; additive, super-additive or suppressive interactions
in behaviour and in the causal effect; adversarial search under a fixed budget, retested on freshly authored
confirmation items.
P9.7 Persistence across tools and precision.
Two hook backends where feasible; bf16 against fp16 and modest quantisation behind a numerical agreement
gate; an effect that depends on an implementation bug is retired.
Gate P9 (G5 for the second model, G6 beyond). Separate conclusions for behaviour, monitor, function and
anatomy. If the function recurs but component identities differ, the heterogeneity is part of the result. If only one
model shows it, a deep single-model case study needs stronger within-model causal proof and a stated reason why it
generalises conceptually; no universal claim about language models is made.
Status (11 Nov 2026): not started; gated on G4. Qwen3-8B (thinking on/off) is not downloaded (open
decision D3).
5.2.11 P10. Mechanism-guided repair and comparative eﬀicacy
Question. Does knowledge of the mechanism yield a repair that beats simple non-mechanistic methods?
Kept as optional practical use (G7); it starts only after P7 yields a specific intervention. A cheap repair that
works is a result in its own right.
P10.1 Operational loss.
Weighted O1/O2 error, role-by-value departures (O4), calibration and OOD robustness, subject to a maxi-
mum degradation on no-cue and relevant-input tasks; never a teacher-forced gold-likelihood statistic alone.
P10.2 Non-mechanistic ladder (first).
The explicit relevance instruction (“identify and ignore irrelevant information”, already a G3 condition),
self-consistency or majority vote, a longer reasoning budget, then a deterministic semantic filter, rephrasing
into governing variables, a small symbolic solver, two-query consistency and targeted counterfactual aug-
mentation; latency, compute and the damage from wrongly ignoring relevant inputs recorded. This ladder
sets the bar.
P10.3 T raining-free circuit interventions.
Conditional replacement, projection of a causal direction, gating of a proven edge, small direction edits,
patching from a matched no-cue rendering; intensity tuned on development only, with a strength-versus-
damage curve and checks on prompts where the same quantity is relevant (the R twin).
P10.4 Monitor-triggered repair.
Only if P5 passes; triggered against universal application under realistic base rates; an oracle trigger is a
non-deployable upper bound.
P10.5 T raining-based mitigation.
If justified, certificate-backed paired consistency training with a correctness loss and relevance-preservation
controls, againstrandomdistractoraugmentation, strong-distractorcurriculaandgenericinstructiontuning;
whole law clusters held out; follow whether the mechanism weakens, relocates or is bypassed.
P10.6 Attack and defence.
Certified adversarial edits under declared attacker access and budget; adaptation curves and fresh-attack
transfer.
P10.7 Causal linkage.
Targeted edit against equal-norm random, nearby-layer, alternative-component and prompt-only baselines
and no edit; a repair that works without the mechanism explaining why is an empirical intervention, not a
Working research protocol – not completed results

######## PAGE 39 ########
PHYSMON | RESEARCH REDESIGN v2 (REVISED 11 NOV 2026) 39
causal account.
Gate P10 (G7). A positive result needs held-out paired improvement in a practically meaningful outcome (prefer-
ably O1, O2 or O4), statistically resolved harm bounds, and an advantage or distinctive trade-off against the non-
mechanistic ladder. If cue removal or the relevance instruction works better with less damage, the neural edit is not
called operationally superior; it may still be a mechanistic test.
Status (11 Nov 2026): not started. A Phase-I reviewer asked for exactly this downstream use; the first
rung (relevance instruction) is measured in G3 at no extra cost.
5.2.12 P11. Confirmatory closure, adversarial review and claim freeze
Question. Can an independent reader reproduce the primary result and state the causal account and the
best attempt to falsify it? Kept; it closes every gate and owns the external confirmation of G6.
P11.1 One causal chain, not the lab log.
Figures follow the claim ladder of Section4.9: the role-by-value design and hypotheses; the measurement
audit (generated answers against likelihood diagnostics); the role-by-value effect on independent structures;
interventions with absolute effects; the path with its counterfactual predictions; replication or repair. Fail-
ures appear in compact explicit tables.
P11.2 Mandatory final audit.
Independent recomputation of the main numbers, validation signatures, code and model versions, con-
tamination audit, preregistration deviations, multiple-testing ledger, negative and zero-row results, exact
intervention sites, intervals, baselines, alternative metrics and the statistical unit; a mechanical check of
every draft’s wording against the claim registry’s prohibited wording; a check that provenance fields (au-
thorship, validation) match what the text says. An unaﬀiliated peer attacks the strongest claim from the
raw evidence and the released protocol.
P11.3 T wo-stage confirmation.
The internal hold-out is used for one explicit confirmatory decision (G4). A fully untouched external cohort,
from the EPC external physics sets or other newly written, law-held-out material, is opened once in G6,
after the hypothesis, functional representation, causal site and inference code are frozen. Any tuning after
opening turns it into development; new data are then needed.
P11.4 Reproducible release.
Prompts, symbolicprograms, certificates, validatorlabels, alleligibleoutputsandlog-probabilities, inclusion
metadata, raw before/after intervention values, code, environment, seeds, hardware and checksums; passing
and failing runs with an explicit authority hierarchy.
P11.5 V enue chosen after the result.
A mechanism narrative needs a substantial new insight; a measurement result takes an evaluation or bench-
mark framing; a mitigation result a robustness framing. The narratives are not kept at equal weight unless
the evidence forms one non-inflated chain.
Gate P11. No submission until an independent reader can reproduce the primary figures and state, in one paragraph,
the causal explanation and the best attempt to falsify it. Disconfirming evidence enters the headline scope, not future
work. Each claim states its validation tier (LLM panel or human expert); without either, results stay exploratory;
any manuscript discloses agent authorship and LLM validation.
Status (11 Nov 2026): the Phase-I paper was withdrawn on 11 November 2026; its reviews and a verification
of the reviewers’ claims are recorded, and no Phase-I claim survives as stated. The claim ledger exists. The
EPC external cohort is not built (October B5, demoted to G6). No venue is chosen.

This section keeps the October edition’s catalogue of 104 registered contrasts (A01–A18, B01–B14, C01–C18,
D01–D16, E01–E18, F01–F20) with its identifiers, so that the Stage 14 journal and ledger still resolve. The

Phase-B and gate contrasts defined there are additional to this list. As in the October edition, the catalogue is
not 104 independent hypothesis tests: contrasts are grouped into preregistered families, screening is separated
from confirmation, a confirmatory subset is selected before the corresponding test cohort is opened, and low-
value branches are stopped early. A negative result removes the branch’s supported claim, not the datum.
Columns. ID carries the October tier under the identifier: R = required on the critical path, C = conditional
on earlier evidence, X = exploratory or high-upside.Contrast is a condensed but faithful restatement of the

• DONE-EXPLORA TOR Y— run in Stage 14 with the cited journal entry; exploratory evidence (data

• OPEN — not run; kept as specified, with the readout of Section4.5;
• REVISED — kept, but its target, outcome or object is changed by the revised core (Section4); the
replacement is stated;
• RETIRED — not run as specified; the reason is stated;
• SUPERSEDED by a named core element that answers the same question more directly.
Every item that rests on the retired legacy label (Slp, base 0, 0.5 nats; retired for v2 analyses in J14.2-011) or
on normalised recovery is marked REVISED (with its replacement outcome among O1–O6) or RETIRED. A
cell or contrast with zero evaluable records isNOT_EVALUATED, never a zero effect.

6.8 Contrasts added by the revision
These core elements of Section4 have no October identifier; they are registered here with their gates.
1. Role-by-value cells per stratum (R, D, C, K where feasible; ≥ 3 values, ≥ 5 with held-out values
for the dependency curve; infeasibility recorded, never imputed). Certificates at G1, discovery at G3, the
preregistered role-by-value family at G4.
2. Multiple phrasings of each role relation (≥ 2 independently validated, at least one without marker words
such as “unrelated” or “separate”); effects must agree across phrasings. G1, G3, G4.
3. Misuse response curves fh(z) for D, C and K cells, with answer matching that keeps every match
(UNIQUE_MATCH, MULTI_MATCH, NO_MATCH). Frozen with the item at G1; read at G3/G4.

7 Twelve decisive experiment cards
The October edition specified twelve cards in priority order, as minimal specifications for an engineer or
research agent. Each has a purpose, a primary outcome, the competing comparators, a no-go response and
an artifact. Those fields are kept below in condensed form. Two fields are added:Status, from the Stage 14
record, andRevision, from the disposition of the first revision and the revised core (Section4). Where the two
disagree, the Revision field governs.
Rule kept from the October edition. An agent must not invent a different estimand or panel mid-run.
The estimands and panels stated in a card’s Revision field are frozen at G1 or when the card’s gate opens; from
then on the same prohibition applies to them. A card with zero evaluable records reportsNOT_EVALUATED,
never a zero effect.

restoring a baseline.

8 Statistical design: standards for inference, not decoration
8.1 Independent unit, estimands and non-independence
The independent unit for a primary claim is the independently authored symbolic structure or template clus-
ter, not a rendered prompt, paraphrase, numeric value, phrasing or decoder sample. Values, phrasings, roles,
samples and models are repeated measures nested in structures; counting them as independent is pseudorepli-
cation. For generalisation to new laws or domains, the law or domain cluster is the sampling unit, or the
population is declared fixed and inference conditional on it; with only a few domains, no asymptoticp-values
are reported as if there were many.
Primary behavioural estimands (Section 4.3), per model and structure, averaged over structures:
• Inappropriate dependence in stratum D (separately C, K), co-primary (F1): the tracking loss ¯TN − ¯TD
against the non-numeric sentence over all attempted samples (the loss against the no-cue prompt beside
it), which any departure outside tolerance lowers whatever its sign; the misuse shares against their rates
under N attribute it (secondary family).
• Inadequate responsiveness in stratum R, co-primary (F2): the neglect share (R samples answering the
irrelevant-role value) against the placebo match rate in the same cell, beside¯TR.
• Role-by-value interaction, co-primary (F3): the role × value term of a mixed-effects logistic model of
tracking; physics predicts no dependence of tracking onz in either role.
• Descriptive: λR, λD and Λ with the multimodality guard of Section4.3; they gate nothing.
• Presence: O1 difference between the non-numeric sentence and a D cell, for comparison with the numeric-
salience literature.
Each estimand is reported per phrasing and pooled over phrasings; a role claim needs agreement across
phrasings. Population-average and population-specific results (Section 4.6) are both reported; results on
reliably solved or model-positive items are selected on the outcome and do not generalise to all items. Eligibility
(completeness, feasibility, population membership) is recorded before any intervention or cue condition is
scored, and no-cue and relevant-role (R) performance is always measured beside the cue conditions.Causal
estimands are the interactionIh of Section4.8 under a declared claim type; an activation intervention is not
the natural indirect effect of the quantity.Monitoring (G7 only): out-of-sample paired difference in a proper
score at a fixed information budget, AUROC as a ranking metric.
Working research protocol – not completed results

######## PAGE 54 ########
PHYSMON | RESEARCH REDESIGN v2 (REVISED 11 NOV 2026) 54
8.2 Intervals, tests and their assumptions
Samples and values are first reduced to structure-level estimates; the primary analysis is then a paired analysis
of the J structure-level differences: a t-interval with J − 1 degrees of freedom, and a sign-flip randomisation
test whose validity rests on the symmetry of the paired differences under the null (checked and reported).
The k × N draws are never pooled as independent (Miller 2024). Hierarchical modelling (mixed-effects logistic
or linear models with structure, value and phrasing effects, simplified when singular; Matuschek et al.) and
cluster resampling (bootstrap over structures, 2,000 resamples, seed 42, as in Stage 14) are complementary
views, not a ranking: atJ of a few dozen, CLT and bootstrap intervals can under-cover (Bowyer et al., ICML
2025), and a clustered Bayesian interval is reported beside them. For binary rates: denominators always,
Wilson or clustered intervals; for model comparisons on the same structures: paired analyses. Calibration
claims (G7) follow the October rules: reliability curves with bin support, ECE with fixed declared bins plus
an adaptive variant, never “best calibrated” from one metric.
Cue-induced changes are read against the self-flip floor measured in G2 (two independent draws under the
same condition), never against zero.
8.3 Effect sizes, equivalence and the language of null results
Every contrast has a smallest effect of scientific interest (SESOI) stated in G1with its reason, not chosen for
a convenient sample size, and in the units of the estimand it applies to. For the D tracking loss and misuse
shares the reason is behavioural: the share of answers that may be lost to an irrelevant quantity before it
matters (planning value 0.10 in tracking); for the R neglect share above its placebo rate the same 0.10 (a
tenth of R answers ignoring a quantity that matters); for the F3 role× value interaction an odds ratio of
1.5 per value step on tracking (planning), because a smaller value dependence would not change a reading of
any single item; for descriptiveλD a leak of a tenth of the relevant-role response; for tracking shares and O1
differences the reason states which use the result serves (a reliability claim may care about a few percentage
points; a costly mechanism study needs an effect large enough to localise). Equivalence is claimed only by two
one-sided tests within the SESOI, with adequate power: withω the standard deviation of the per-structure
difference, about 8.6 ω2/∆2 structures give 80% power when the true effect is zero; atω = 0 .2, ∆ = 0 .10
needs about 34 structures and∆ = 0 .05 about 137. If the sample cannot support the margin, the outcome is
INCONCLUSIVE, and the sample size, not the margin, is what G1 revises before confirmation. Four outcomes
are kept distinct in all text: an effect (interval excludes zero and extends beyond the margin), a trivial effect
(interval excludes zero but lies inside the margin), equivalence (interval inside the margin and including zero),
and inconclusive (none of these). “No effect” is never written for an inconclusive result.
Rare categories. Misuse-curve and copy matches may be rare (Stage 14.20 had 2 wrong answers in 128
cells). Their rates are estimated per structure with a Jeffreys Beta prior (zero counts give a finite rate with
a proper interval), combined across structures with a Beta-Binomial hierarchical model, and reported with
denominators; a contrast between rare rates is never read from a structure-pooled count.
8.4 Multiple comparisons and research degrees of freedom
• G3 is estimation; its scorecard is not a test.
• G4 tests the role-by-value family as three co-primary contrasts, Holm-corrected at family-wiseα = 0 .05:
(F1) inappropriate dependence in D, the tracking loss ¯TN − ¯TD against the non-numeric sentence (one-
sided, since a departure in any direction lowers tracking); (F2)inadequate responsiveness in R, the neglect
share against its placebo rate (one-sided); (F3) therole-by-value interaction, the role × value term of a
mixed-effects logistic model of tracking (two-sided: physics predicts tracking that does not depend onz
in either role). For H6-RD each of F1–F3 is instead tested for equivalence within its SESOI.Λ and λ
are reported as descriptive summaries and gate nothing. The misuse shares that attribute an F1 loss to
particular misuse curves are a secondary family, Holm-corrected across curves and tested in each curve’s
predicted direction, only after F1 passes. The second model follows by fixed sequence after the first. At
most one secondary family chosen in G3 is tested after the primary family, Holm-corrected, and labelled
as chosen on EXPLORATION data.
• Prespecified secondary scans use Benjamini–Hochberg and stay exploratory.
• Selection over layers, heads, sites, positions, phrasings, metrics and thresholds is handled by discovery on
one set and a single evaluation on an independent set, never by reporting the best of many tests.
• If queue delays force G4 into batches, one interim analysis at half the sample with Lan–DeMets O’Brien–
Fleming spending may be preregistered.
Working research protocol – not completed results

######## PAGE 55 ########
PHYSMON | RESEARCH REDESIGN v2 (REVISED 11 NOV 2026) 55
8.5 Power and precision protocol
Before G3 and again before G4, simulate from the G2 estimates (structure, value and phrasing variance
components, ω of the cue difference, within-item Bernoulli variance, which more samples reduce and between-
structure variance does not; Wang 2026), forJ ∈ { 24, 40, 60, 80} complete role-by-value structures andk ∈
{3, 5, 8}, at least 1,000 simulated datasets each analysed exactly as planned, on simulated null data as well
as effect data so that the type-I error of the chosen analysis and resampling unit is shown to be calibrated,
for the tracking loss, the role-by-value interaction and the misuse, neglect and copy shares, which may be
rare (Stage 14.20 had 2 wrong answers in 128 cells). The simulation includes a scenario with 20–40% loss to
infeasible cells, validation failures, parse failures and budget exhaustion. Analytic bracket:J ≈ 7.85 ω2/δ2
for 80% power at two-sidedα = 0 .05 (Miller 2024), about 6.2 ω2/δ2 for the one-sided G4 tests, withω the
standard deviation of the per-structure valueof the estimand being tested (estimated in G2, not borrowed
from a no-cue difference); withω = 0.25, δ = 0.10 needs about 49 (two-sided) or 39 (one-sided) structures and
δ = 0.15 about 22 or 17. More samples per item cannot substitute for more independent structures. If errors
are genuinely rare, the legitimate choices are a harder, independently justified regime or the study of correct
selection (H6); a continuous diagnostic (O6) is never promoted to proof of an error because the categorical
endpoint lacks power. The October planning allocation of 300–600 structures is withdrawn: the number is
whatever the simulation requires for the decisions actually made.
8.6 Negative and missing result policy
A zero-row job, failed hook, timeout, budget-exhausted or format-invalid response, infeasible cell, ineligible
item or untested control isNOT_EVALUATED, not a null effect. A missingness codebook records reason, first seen,
planned run, attempts, eligible population and intended analysis. Exclusions and completeness are reported
by condition, role, value, phrasing and model. Every primary contrast is reported three ways: all attempted
samples with non-complete records as “not correct” (O1), complete-case, and with budget-exhausted records
counted as wrong (a bound; answers at the length limit are almost always wrong in published reasoning
evaluations, Hochlehnert et al.). Data-dependent missing values are never replaced by zero or negative labels.
9 Compute, human effort, storage and reproducibility architecture
This section keeps the October edition’s requirements that are still valid (measure before budgeting, data
contracts, a conceptual preflight, storage discipline, independent human validation) and replaces its generic
seven-step compute ladder by a budget staged on the revised gates (Section 5.1). Tags: [V] checked in
repository files or job records;[ENV] measured cluster or stack constraint;[I] planning arithmetic or design
choice. Every figure below that is not tagged[V] or [ENV] is a planning number, not a result.
9.1 Environment as it stands (11 November 2026)
Hardware and scheduler [ENV]. The pabitra account is shared with other projects, and their jobs count
against the same per-user QoS caps: H100 1 GPU, 12 CPU, 300G; A100 2 GPUs; H200 2 GPUs, 12 CPU,
300G. sbatch --test-only does not model these caps, so the account’s other jobs (squeue -u pabitra ) are
added by hand before a partition is chosen; live Slurm output outranks any dated snapshot. Measured H100
queue waits were about 38 hours (job 417416) to about 6 days (job 425243). Weight loading from/scratch
took about 7 minutes for Qwen3-32B (job 417416) and has taken up to about half an hour for 7–8B models;
walltime is budgeted for it. The October edition’s warning stands: throughput is measured on Sharanga, never
invented.
Storage roots [V]. Models live under ${PHYSMON_MODEL_ROOT} (default $SCRATCH/models, i.e.
/scratch/pabitra/models), resolved at load time; activations, Slurm logs and large intermediates live
under /scratch/pabitra/physmon. The October 2026 scratch wipe destroyed the Phase-I activation tensors;
the analyses that depended on them areNOT_EVALUATED and are not reconstructed from stand-ins. Scratch is
treated as non-reconstructable runtime storage, never as an archive.
Software provenance [V]. Pinned model manifests (revision, per-file sha256, architecture and compatibil-
ity checks) are in docs/model_manifests/; the registry is docs/model_registry.yml. Job templates set
PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1 so that no user-site package leaks into the pinned environment (docs/environment_-
lock.yml; TransformerLens 3.4.0).gpunode6 has no usablegit, so every job carriesSUBMIT_COMMIT (the full
SHA from the submission node) and refuses to run without a commit; all jobs of one study step run from one
Working research protocol – not completed results

Before any further Qwen3-32B run its revision is identified and a manifest written. If the scratch file hashes
match a published revision, that is recorded as an after-the-fact identification, not as a pin at run time. Qwen3-
32B is used only in bf16 (TransformerLens 3.4boot() defaults to float32), through plain forward hooks or the
TransformerBridge, with exact patching only, after a parity test.
Generation engine (open decision D4). Plain Hugging Facegenerate gave Qwen3-32B about 20 tokens/s
aggregate with no gain from batch 2 to batch 3, far below the memory-bandwidth bound. KV memory does not
explain this: at about 256 KiB per token, the 10–18 GB left after the bf16 weights hold roughly 40,000–70,000
tokens, i.e. several 6,000-token sequences. A faster engine is therefore expected to help, but is not measured
here. If vLLM is approved it is installed in a separateuv environment (its wheels bundle their own torch), after
a check of the cluster’s CUDA driver, followed by a logit and greedy-output parity check against the pinned
Hugging Face stack on fixed prompts and a short on-cluster timing job, before any study run. Generation and
analysis are split: vLLM generates and saves token ids; activations and every teacher-forced quantity come
from a Hugging Face teacher-forced forward pass over the saved sequences, so hooks never run inside vLLM.
Without vLLM the plan runs on the 7–8B models.

9.4 Staged budget for the revised gates
Generations per model= structures × cells per structure× k samples. A “core cell” below is one role-by-value
cell (role× value × phrasing); the minimum complete structure has R and D at three values in two phrasings,
i.e. 12 cells, plus the no-cue base and the non-numeric sentence: 14 cells. An added ablation condition is
assumed to be crossed with three values and two phrasings (6 cells). The HF column multiplies by the
measured 12.6–14.7 s per record; the vLLM column isan estimate scaled from published single-H100
benchmarks (thousands of output tokens/s for 7–8B models, hundreds for 32B in bf16; the first revision
estimated about 1 hour for 5,120 7–8B generations), not a measurement, and is replaced by the on-cluster
parity and timing job.

Rules for the budget. (1) Jobs are sized to finish in under 10 hours with an internal time budget (the runner
stops cleanly; unrun records are NOT_EVALUATED), because 1–6-day queue waits make long jobs that die at
walltime expensive; a step that exceeds that is split into condition blocks from one frozen commit. (2) Sampled
and greedy records are never pooled. (3) Qwen3-32B enters only as a hard-subset check; without vLLM it is
run, if at all, on that small subset. (4) The thinking budget is part of the contract (12,288 tokens truncated
9–12% of Qwen3-32B records), and truncation is an outcome (O3), not a reason to drop a record. (5) The
October edition’s behavioural cost model remains the template: structures× values × phrasings × cells ×
models × (scored forwards + generated samples), with the output-format wrappers recorded separately.
9.5 Human effort
Independent physics review (block B4) is the binding non-GPU cost; until human reviewers are available, the
qualified LLM panel of Section3.7 provides the interim tier (its models are open decision D2). Generating
and certifying structures is agent and CPU work; review is not. Planning figure: 15–20 minutes per structure
per reviewer.

Until human reviewers are available, G4 items are validated by the qualified LLM panel (Section3.7): roughly
2–3 judge runs of two passes per structure, a few GPU-hours locally or an API budget, plus recorded adju-
dication of split verdicts (adjudicated items reported separately). Without a qualified panel, G4 is reported
as EXPLORATORY-REPLICATION. The authoring agent’s own review is not validation, and agent authorship and
LLM validation are disclosed. The October edition’s staﬀing roles are kept (hypotheses and claim ledger;
generator and symbolic verifier; instrumentation and reproducibility; validator coordination; an independent
reviewer who attacks leakage and causal interpretation); roles can be combined, but independence checks
cannot all be done by the agent that wrote the data. Its 400-structure, 800-judgment validation budget is
withdrawn with the demotion of large-scale DECOY-v2 scaling: only the structures G3 and G4 need are
generated and reviewed.
9.6 Storage
Kept from the October edition: persist normalised per-structure, per-cell raw records and complete model
provenance in the repository; store activation caches transiently on scratch with an object index and hashes;
keep only discovery-critical activation slices plus reproducible extraction scripts; use safetensors, zarr or HDF5
(no pickled code in shared artifacts); pin dtype, shape and named hook coordinates; log when a cache came
from an earlier model revision; make every run restartable and idempotent (raw records flushed after every
batch, run_summary.json with a sha256 of the records, used output directories refused).
Activation memory is recomputed for current models fromnitems × npositions × nlayers × dmodel× bytes, not
copied from Phase I. Illustration[I]: one residual-stream site in bf16 is3584 × 2 × 28 ≈ 196 KiB per token
for Qwen2.5-7B and 4096 × 2 × 32 = 256 KiB per token for Llama-3.1-8B, i.e. roughly 0.4–0.5 GiB for one
2,048-token trace at every layer. Reasoning traces therefore make all-position caching impractical; G5 caches
only the positions and sites a card names, recomputing from saved token ids when needed.
9.7 Machine-readable data contracts
Every raw record carries the October fields still in use:run_id, phase_id (now the gate),exploratory_-
or_confirmatory, structure_uuid, template_cluster_id, symbolic_program_hash, cue_type, cue_se-
mantic_role, cue_numeric_value, unit_type, numeric_proximity, digit_overlap, cue_position, isola-
tion_condition, model_id, model_commit, tokenizer_commit, chat_template, answer_wrapper_id, gen-
erated_answer_raw, parsed_answer, parse_status, correctness, seed, dtype, wall_time, artifact_-
checksum. The October likelihood fields (target_answer_ids, target_span_start/end, gold_logprob_-
raw/per_token, alternative_scores) are kept only on records that compute the O6 diagnostic.
Added by the revised framework: stratum (R, D, C, K),role_relation_id, value_index and value
z, phrasing_id and marker_word_present, certified_response y∗ r (z), tracking T, feasibility_status,
misuse_matches (UNIQUE_MATCH/MULTI_MATCH/NO_MATCH with every matched hypothesis),completion_sta-
tus (O3), thinking_closed, generated_tokens, token_budget, relative_error, the three grading views
and the per-viewsource_ambiguous flag, unit_stated_in_prompt, sampling parameters (temperature, top-
p, top-k, sample index), contract_version, data_role, population, submit_commit, model_manifest_-
sha256, engine and its version (HF or vLLM), andoom_fallback; created_by, verified_by and admis-
sion_category on every item.
Causal records add the October fields ( receiver_id, donor_id, edit_site, edit_semantics, scale,
clean/corrupt_definition, hook_tensor_shape, absolute_Y_control, absolute_Y_intervened, KL_dam-
age, model_positive_eligibility, recipient generation outcomes) plus claim_type (T1, T2, T3; Sec-
tion 4.8), the declared metric, the clean cue effect beside the interactionIh, the ablation kind (resample,
interchange, mean), noising or denoising, and the matched-random-component null. Every derived table
names its source manifest and calculation commit.

Continuous-integration checks (October list, kept): invariant answer across nuisance edits; correct an-
swer change under certified relevant edits; only the declared spans mutated; exact-duplicate and cluster-split
integrity; no train/test structure or cluster collisions; leakage-free preprocessing; out-of-fold scores; identi-
cal denominators for paired models; no zero-row result read as a zero effect; hooks removed after each run;
no gradients accumulated; no confirmatory run with a development-fitted threshold.Added: every D, C,
K cell certified invariant and every R cell certified responsive over its declared range; feasibility recorded,
never imputed; phrasings without marker words present; a record notCOMPLETE never graded WRONG; greedy
and sampled records never pooled; every model in a run has a manifest, or its records carrymodel_commit
NOT_RECORDED.
9.8 Preflight skeleton
Conceptual validation contract, not a runnable implementation; it extends the October skeleton with the
manifest, engine-parity and feasibility steps.
# Conceptual validation contract (revised); not runnable code.
manifest = freeze_structural_splits(certified_role_by_value_structures)
assert no_cluster_overlap(manifest.discovery, manifest.confirmation)
assert no_cluster_overlap(manifest.confirmation, manifest.external)
record_feasibility(manifest) # R, D, C, K per structure; never imputed
for model in selected_models:
require_pinned_manifest(model) # docs/model_manifests/, else NOT_RECORDED
validate_native_chat_template(model)
validate_hook_parity(model, sites=planned_sites, length=planned_trace_length)
if engine(model) == "vllm":
validate_engine_parity(model, reference="pinned HF stack")
run_timing_job(model) # replaces planning rates
for model in selected_models:
for group in manifest.discovery: # design-validation pilot first, then G3
records = generate_all_preregistered_cells(model, group, k_samples)
assert certified_invariance_and_response(records.certificates)
emit_immutable_raw_records(records, submit_commit)
# Freeze choices using discovery ONLY.
# G4 family is fixed in G1; discovery may add one secondary family
protocol = freeze_g4_family(manifest.discovery)
power = simulate_power(protocol, variance_components_from_G2)
write_preregistration(protocol, power, git_sha=submit_commit)
# Confirmation panel is loaded ONCE by a frozen script.
result = evaluate_frozen_protocol(protocol, manifest.confirmation)
report_cluster_robust_effects_and_all_units(result) # NOT_EVALUATED kept apart
# Unsuccessful results never silently reroute to a new confirmatory test.
if not result.passes_prespecified_gate:
close_claim_and_open_new_discovery_branch(protocol, result)
10 Conditional decisions: how to react if the evidence is un-
favourable
The October edition’s decision table is kept where its rule still applies, re-indexed to the revised gates (Sec-
tion 5.1); rows that named the retired head-11 starting point or the retired signed likelihood label are gener-
alised to any component or likelihood metric. The revision’s contingencies follow in a second table. Every row
is decided before the data it applies to are seen.

Stop–pivot hierarchy (October edition, kept): credibility of the measured effect outranks benchmark size;
causal interpretation outranks component count; reproducible out-of-cluster prediction outranks peak discrim-
ination scores; selective correctness improvement outranks ratio recovery. The plan is adaptive about which
branch is investigated, not about rewriting confirmatory statistics after outcomes.

11 Literature-grounded positioning and novelty test
The October map of sources to design (its entries L01–L25 remain in the bibliography, Section14) is kept.
This edition adds the work that appeared or was found by the searches of 11 November 2026 and restates the
novelty claim more narrowly. Absence of a related work from a selective search is not proof that none exists;
every source must be read in full before it is used to claim novelty; “first to show” is never written unless
verified against the full adjacent literature. Venue status was established by opening the venue or arXiv page;
“per arXiv” means only the arXiv comment claims the venue.
11.1 Closest work and what PhysMon must add
Work What it already contributes What PhysMon must add to be distinct
PRISM-Physics (Zhao et

Physics benchmarks found without irrelevant-quantity tests (per their abstracts): UGPhysics (ICML 2025),

SeePhys.
11.2 What could actually be novel (conditional claims)
N1 (revised). A role-by-value behavioural account on certified physics strata: whether a model’s answers
follow the certified dependence on a quantity’s value (invariant for D, C, K; the certified response for
R) across phrasings, separated from numeral salience, plausibility, unit, position and marker wording,
and contrasted with a non-physics dependency control.Risk: if the pattern matches GSM-DC or NoOp
behaviour in math, the physics framing adds little.
N2. A mechanistically predictive function for how physical role gates a quantity’s use (or how correct selection
is implemented, H6), established under the causal standard of Section4.8 on held-out structures and a
second model. Risk: it reduces to operation planning (Qu and Gomes), anchoring (Owusu et al.) or
readout copying (Liu).
N3 (demoted). Whether a single-prompt internal monitor adds information beyond deployable comparators
under cluster-held-out evaluation.Risk: small; G7 only.
N4. A selective intervention that improves certified invariance or accuracy without damaging relevant use and
beats cheap alternatives.Risk: a raw accuracy gain without mechanistic linkage belongs to robust training.
N5 (new, modest). A documented case of how teacher-forced string likelihood misled a physics-reliance
study (the Phase-I lesson), supported by the reviewers’ reproduced audit and Stage 14; consistent with
evidence that what models encode and what they say can diverge (Yuchi, Du and Eisner, EACL 2026).
Novelty falsification before any submission. Re-run targeted searches (certified physics distractor; phys-
ical relevance counterfactual; role-by-value; numerical competition heads; operation planning distractor; an-
choring circuits; readout copying; causal abstraction scientific reasoning); inspect experiment tables and code
of every close hit; keep closest_work_matrix.csv with year and venue, generator, formal guarantee, be-
havioural target, models, localisation method, functional evidence, external validity and intervention.
12 The first execution sprint
The October sprint (tag and reproduce Phase I; base-rotation attack; scoring interface; structure overlap;
validator qualification; typed generator; pilot) was executed as Stages 14.0–14.19 (AppendixA), except that
validator qualification stopped at materials and the user’s review of the planted-defect bank, and the physicist
review was replaced by agent verification at the user’s instruction of 26 October 2026. The next sprint
is ordered by which uncertainty would make later work meaningless. Items 1–5 need no GPU; nothing is
submitted without the user’s acceptance of the exact command.

13 Proposed paper architectures depending on the evidence
The October edition proposed three architectures: a causal mechanism paper (A, high bar), a measurement
paper on what certified counterfactuals measure (B), and a mechanism-guided robustness paper (C). They
are mapped here onto the revised hypotheses (Section4.7) and claim hierarchy (Section4.9). Which paper is
written is decided by the evidence; the venue is chosen after the result, not before. None of these architectures
is a plan to obtain a particular outcome.

14 Bibliography and primary-source links
Provenance of the entries. Entries [L01]–[L30] are the October edition’s bibliography, kept with its
numbering, venues and URLs exactly as given there (located and cross-checked against publisher, author-
project or arXiv pages on 14 October 2026; “preprint” means not independently verified as peer-reviewed at
that date). Entries [N01]– were added on 11 November 2026 from the revision’s literature search (three
search agents). Their venue status is marked as the revision marks it: [R] the venue or arXiv page was
opened by a search agent and the entry confirmed;per arXiv only the arXiv comment claims the venue;[R,
re-opened] additionally re-opened by the planning agent (the two entries closest to the novelty boundary).
Entries listed by the revision without either mark are given as listed and areunverified here. Where the
revision gives no URL, only the arXiv identifier is given, and where it gives neither, only the citation as listed;
no URL is supplied from memory. Every source must be read in full before it is used to claim or deny novelty;
absence from this list is not proof that no similar work exists.

15 Definition of scientific completion
Amanuscriptisscientificallyreadyonlyafterthegatethatitscentralclaimneedshasbeenpassed(Section 5.1),
and only at the level of the claim hierarchy (Section4.9) that the evidence reaches: a behavioural role effect
needs G4; a causal-mediation claim needs T3, or T2 with the controls of Section4.8, at G5; a mechanism claim
needs G5 with rescue, causal abstraction and held-out prediction; a generalisation claim needs G6. Readiness
is judged on independently verifiable artifacts, and the manuscript must be able to answer every question
below.
1. Construct. What model behaviour changed, in which outcome (O1–O6), in which stratum (R, D, C,
K) and population, and why must the physical answer be invariant (D, C, K) or respond by the certified
amount (R)? Which separate tests establish the natural-language physical validity of the items and their
match to the encoded graph, and was that validation independent (G1; B4 review at G4)?
2. Alternatives. Which weaker account was strongest — generic perturbation (H0), numeral presence or
plausibility and unit (H1, H2), length or diversion (H5), string-scoring, format or diﬀiculty artifacts — and
where was it falsified, including by the non-physics control?
3. Role by value. Does the model keep its answers fixed where a quantity is irrelevant (no tracking loss, no
misuse) and follow the certified response where it is relevant (no neglect), as the physics requires, across
values and across phrasings with and without marker words; are misuse hypotheses supported only by
curves across several values, with all matches kept?
4. Computation. If a mechanism is claimed: which computation was identified under a declared claim type
(T1, T2, T3), beyond the effect of removing a component, with the interaction estimandIh and the clean
cue effect reported side by side?
5. F alsifiable predictions. Which intervention predictions, committed before the test, would have failed if
the account were false, and what happened on held-out structures, values and the second model?
6. Scope. Which models, budgets, strata, conditions and thinking settings do and do not replicate, and which
models were uninformative because they fell outside the diﬀiculty band?
7. Monitoring and repair (only if claimed, G7). Did a monitor add information beyond fair, cheap, deploy-
able baselines on unseen clusters; can an intervention improve O1 or O2 without disrupting legitimately
relevant quantities, against the relevance instruction and a cheap filter?
8. Reproducibility .Can an independent researcher reproduce successes and nulls, with denominators, ex-
clusions andNOT_EVALUATED cells, from pinned model manifests,SUBMIT_COMMIT-stamped raw records and
the frozen analysis scripts?
9. Novelty . Is the core insight different from GSM-DC, GSM-Symbolic, PRISM-Physics, Qu and Gomes,
Owusu, Wiegreffe and Feldman, Liu, numerical-heuristic accounts and existing causal interpretability work,
and is any overlap stated?
10. W ording.Does the manuscript say no more than the evidence supports, as checked by the wording script
against the claim registry and the evidence ledger, with agent authorship and agent verification disclosed?
Consequences. If (4) or (5) cannot be answered, the project can still produce rigorous measurement science
(a behavioural role paper, a certified null, a cost result or the methodology paper of Section13), but it is
not presented as a mechanistic explanation. If (1) fails, the work returns to the construct and measurement
definition, however strong other results look. A certified null (H0 with equivalence shown against a margin
fixed before the data and an adequately powered design) and a cost finding (H5) are complete results; an
inconclusive interval, an underpowered contrast or zero evaluable rows are not, and are reported as what they
are. Results without LLM-panel or human validation are complete only as exploratory results.
