D Revision log
14 October 2026 (v2.0). Research redesign replacing the June 2026 Phase-II plan; Phase B added; adopted
as plan of record by the user on 15 October 2026.
11 November 2026, first draft of the revision. Written as a separate Markdown revision layer
(PhysMon_Research_v2.1.md, commit 2cf08e2) from the reviews, Stage 14 and three literature searches.
Working research protocol – not completed results

######## PAGE 73 ########
PHYSMON | RESEARCH REDESIGN v2 (REVISED 11 NOV 2026) 73
An independent agent review against the repository found ten factual errors (among them: hook parity
had already passed in job 399217; the Stage 14 reasoning runner is greedy, so sampling needs a new
contract; a wrong KV-memory explanation of the Qwen3-32B throughput) and twelve design flaws (no cell
varied role alone; the in-system contrast was confounded with unit; correctness conditioned on evaluability;
near cues inside the grading tolerance; a data-dependent equivalence margin; undefined gate thresholds),
all corrected before commit.
11 November 2026, this edition. A second review by an external language model, supplied by the user
and checked by the agent, led to: the four role strata (disconnected, cancelling, conditional) with the rule
that intermediate use of a cancelling or conditional quantity is not an error; the role-by-value design with
a response scaled by the certified relevant-role response, several validated phrasings and misuse response
curves; separate operational, semantic and status outcomes, with truncation requiring budget exhaustion;
near-answer cues kept in correctness and flagged only for source attribution; all foil matches kept; causal
claim types T1–T3; within-structure, value-matched rescue first; three populations; gate fixes (formula hint
not a gate; moderators secondary; G4 family fixed in advance; scorecard instead of first-matching rule);
staged discovery with an 8–12-structure design pilot; a non-physics control in discovery; SESOI with reasons
and four-way null language; PRISM-Physics added to the closest work. An independent agent review of the
assembled LaTeX draft then found that the first role-by-value estimand (a log-elasticity interaction) was
undefined for mixed sampled answers and zero golds and not sign-aligned across structures, that a shared
trace across roles is physically incoherent, that two values cannot separate misuse curves, and that several
sections still carried superseded rules; it was replaced by per-sample tracking, response fractions scaled by
the certified relevant-role response and a role-discrimination index, T1 restricted to prompts that share a
gold, three values per role, and consistent gate rules throughout.
11 November 2026, refinements after a second external review. The user supplied a further review
by the same external model and asked to rely on LLM reviewers for physics validation for now. Changes:
the primary estimands are per-sample tracking (whose loss catches a departure in either direction), misuse
shares with signed, direction-predicting misuse curves and an R neglect share; the response fractionsλ
and the indexΛ are descriptive only, with a multimodality guard; G4 tests three co-primary contrasts (D
tracking loss, R neglect, role× value interaction on tracking) instead of gatekeeping onΛ; mechanism work
uses two interactions,Ipresence (against the non-numeric sentence) andIrole (against the relevant twin with
the same numeral, on a behaviourally comparable outcome), and only the second supports a role-routing
claim; T1 scores the certified answer against a predeclared alternative on one explicitly identified prefix and
excludes no prefix; H6 is split into H6-RD and H6-extended; the primary model is fixed by a prespecified
rule at the end of G2; and a qualified panel of 2–3 independent LLM reviewers from other model families,
qualified on the user-labelled planted-defect bank, is the interim validation tier for G4, with human review
as a later accuracy study. At the user’s choice of 11 November 2026 the plan was consolidated into this
single LaTeX source and PDF; the Markdown revision layer was removed (preserved in Git history).
